analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV is etiologically linked to preventable head and neck cancers, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal among at-risk groups. The study sought to address knowledge gaps in patient-facing HPV education by developing and piloting an interactive HPV vaccination education program tailored to HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused interactive HPV vaccination education program was adapted for patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the adapted program and provided feedback through semi-structured interviews.
analysis.methods: The adapted program was evaluated using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with these frameworks.
analysis.main_results: Participants generally perceived the adapted program as informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the program enhanced participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination, highlighting the importance of intuitive design, real-person content, and training in evaluating health information.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that digital health interventions for HPV vaccination education can be optimized by incorporating user-centered design elements and content featuring real individuals to improve engagement and effectiveness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a small pilot study with qualitative feedback, which constrains generalizability and precludes causal inference; the strength of evidence is therefore low.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study adapted an interactive HPV vaccination education program originally designed for cervical cancer patients to serve HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients as health educators. Using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument, the authors evaluated participant feedback collected via semi-structured interviews. Participants reported that the adapted program was informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules praised for clarity, organization, accessibility, and cultural appropriateness. Key motivators included physician recommendations and a desire to protect others, while feedback identified areas for improvement in technology, content, and functionality. The authors conclude that effective digital interventions should incorporate training in evaluating health information, intuitive design, and real-person content. However, the study’s small sample and qualitative design limit generalizability and causal inference, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: HPV is etiologically linked to preventable head and neck cancers, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal among at-risk groups. The study sought to address knowledge gaps in patient-facing HPV education by developing and piloting an interactive HPV vaccination education program tailored to HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused interactive HPV vaccination education program was adapted for patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the adapted program and provided feedback through semi-structured interviews.
analysis_en.methods: The adapted program was evaluated using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with these frameworks.
analysis_en.main_results: Participants generally perceived the adapted program as informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the program enhanced participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination, highlighting the importance of intuitive design, real-person content, and training in evaluating health information.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that digital health interventions for HPV vaccination education can be optimized by incorporating user-centered design elements and content featuring real individuals to improve engagement and effectiveness.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a small pilot study with qualitative feedback, which constrains generalizability and precludes causal inference; the strength of evidence is therefore low.

papers.title_zh: 为口咽癌患者和医疗保健提供者开发交互式 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 教育计划:从目标用户反馈中吸取的教训
papers.source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is associated with multiple head and neck cancers, many of which are preventable with the 9-valent HPV vaccine. We developed an interactive HPV vaccination education program (IHVEP) to equip patients with HPV-associated cancers to serve as health educators. Objective: To pilot test the adapted IHVEP, evaluate its content using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM) instrument, and identify factors relevant to optimizing digital health interventions. Methods: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused IHVEP was adapted for patients with oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the program and participated in semi-structured interviews. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with the IMB and SAM frameworks. Results: Participants generally perceived the adapted IHVEP as informative, motivating, and empowering. Key motivators included physician recommendation and a desire to protect others. The program appeared to enhance participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination. Modules were described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate. Feedback identified areas for improvement related to technology, content, and functionality. Conclusions: Findings suggest that effective digital health interventions may benefit from incorporating training in evaluating health information, ensuring intuitive design and navigation, and including content featuring real individuals. These results will inform further refinement of IHVEP and the development of future digital health interventions.

papers.title: Epidemiology and genotype distribution of cervical high-risk human papillomavirus infection among women in Punjab, India: A large-scale retrospective analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: The study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) among women in Punjab region and to assess the association between single/multiple HPV infections and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Materials and Methods: The study involved retrospective analysis of electronic health records for individuals, for which cervical samples were tested for HPV DNA using a real-time polymerase chain reaction assay (Seegene assay) between January 2023 and July 2025. The study included females participating in out-campus screening camps and those attending the department of preventive oncology for routine screening and consenting to undergo HPV testing. Results: Overall HPV prevalence in the study population was 13.8% (544/3919). The most common genotypes were HPV-16 (35.7%), HPV-18 (14%), and HPV-66 (11%). Single genotype infections were most frequent (66.5%). The peak prevalence occurred in women of age group 36–40 years. Multiple HPV infections were significantly associated with higher CIN 2/3 lesions (χ 2 = 4.6; P = 0.032; odds ratio [OR] = 2.8). HPV-16 women had higher, though nonsignificant odds of developing high-grade CIN (OR = 1.96; P = 0.09). HPV-66-positive women had lower odds of developing high-grade CIN, though statistically nonsignificant (OR = 0.47; P = 0.33). Conclusions: There is substantial HPV burden in local population with HPV-16 and HPV-18 as the dominant genotypes. The unexpected high frequency of HPV-66 genotype warrants further molecular and epidemiological investigations. The study findings reinforce the need for implementing systematic large-scale HPV vaccination and HPV screening and molecular testing programs in India to achieve the World Health Organization’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

The study involved retrospective analysis of electronic health records for individuals, for which cervical samples were tested for HPV DNA using a real-time polymerase chain reaction assay (Seegene assay) between January 2023 and July 2025. The study included females participating in out-campus screening camps and those attending the department of preventive oncology for routine screening and consenting to undergo HPV testing. Overall HPV prevalence in the study population was 13.8% (544/3919). The most common genotypes were HPV-16 (35.7%), HPV-18 (14%), and HPV-66 (11%). Single genotype infections were most frequent (66.5%). The peak prevalence occurred in women of age group 36–40 years. Multiple HPV infections were significantly associated with higher CIN 2/3 lesions (χ 2 = 4.6; P = 0.032; odds ratio [OR] = 2.8). HPV-16 women had higher, though nonsignificant odds of developing high-grade CIN (OR = 1.96; P = 0.09). HPV-66-positive women had lower odds of developing high-grade CIN, though statistically nonsignificant (OR = 0.47; P = 0.33). There is substantial HPV burden in local population with HPV-16 and HPV-18 as the dominant genotypes. The unexpected high frequency of HPV-66 genotype warrants further molecular and epidemiological investigations. The study findings reinforce the need for implementing systematic large-scale HPV vaccination and HPV screening and molecular testing programs in India to achieve the World Health Organization’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health burden of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) in the Punjab region by quantifying prevalence and genotype distribution and examining links between infection patterns and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). It aimed to fill local surveillance gaps to inform vaccination and screening strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted using electronic health records from women attending out-campus screening camps or the department of preventive oncology who consented to HPV testing between January 2023 and July 2025.
analysis.methods: Cervical samples were tested for HPV DNA using a real-time polymerase chain reaction assay (Seegene assay). Genotype-specific associations with CIN 2/3 lesions were assessed using chi-square tests and logistic regression to estimate odds ratios.
analysis.main_results: Overall HPV prevalence was 13.8% (544/3919). The most common genotypes were HPV-16 (35.7%), HPV-18 (14%), and HPV-66 (11%). Single genotype infections were most frequent (66.5%). Multiple HPV infections were significantly associated with higher CIN 2/3 lesions (χ2 = 4.6; P = 0.032; OR = 2.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the substantial local HPV burden as dominated by HPV-16 and HPV-18, consistent with global patterns, and highlighted the unexpectedly high frequency of HPV-66 as a novel finding requiring further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the implementation of systematic large-scale HPV vaccination and screening programs in India to advance toward the WHO’s cervical cancer elimination goals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and reliance on routine screening data limit causal inference and generalizability; evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection and information biases.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study in Punjab, India, quantified high-risk HPV prevalence at 13.8% among 3,919 women tested between 2023 and 2025, identifying HPV-16 (35.7%), HPV-18 (14%), and HPV-66 (11%) as the most common genotypes. Single infections predominated (66.5%), but multiple infections were significantly associated with higher-grade CIN 2/3 lesions (OR 2.8, P = 0.032). HPV-16 carriers showed elevated, though nonsignificant, odds of high-grade CIN (OR 1.96, P = 0.09), while HPV-66 showed lower, nonsignificant odds (OR 0.47, P = 0.33). The authors emphasize the need for expanded HPV vaccination and screening to meet WHO elimination targets, noting the unexpectedly high HPV-66 frequency as a novel observation warranting further study.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2023 年 1 月至 2025 年 7 月期间参加校外筛查营或预防肿瘤科并同意接受 HPV 检测的女性的电子健康记录进行回顾性分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时聚合酶链反应测定(Seegene 测定)对宫颈样本进行 HPV DNA 检测。使用卡方检验和逻辑回归来评估与 CIN 2/3 病变的基因型特异性关联,以估计比值比。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体 HPV 患病率 为 13.8% (544/3919)。最常见的基因型是 HPV-16 (35.7%)、HPV-18 (14%) 和 HPV-66 (11%)。单基因型感染最常见(66.5%)。多重 HPV 感染与较高的 CIN 2/3 病变显着相关(χ2 = 4.6;P = 0.032;OR = 2.8)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将当地大量 HPV 负担解释为以 HPV-16 和 HPV-18 为主,这与全球模式一致,并强调 HPV-66 出人意料的高频率是一项需要进一步研究的新发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在印度实施系统性大规模 HPV 疫苗接种 和筛查计划,以推进世界卫生组织的 宫颈癌 消除目标。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 回顾性设计和对常规筛查数据的依赖限制了因果推断和普遍性;由于潜在的选择和信息偏差,证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:本研究旨在确定旁遮普地区女性高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的感染率与基因型,并评估单一/多重HPV感染与宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN)的关联。材料与方法:本研究回顾性分析了2023年1月至2025年7月期间通过实时聚合酶链反应(Seegene试剂盒)检测HPV DNA的宫颈样本的电子健康记录。研究对象包括参与院外筛查营的女性及前往预防肿瘤学科室进行常规筛查并同意接受HPV检测的女性。结果:研究人群中HPV总体患病率为13.8%(544/3919)。最常见基因型为HPV-16(35.7%)、HPV-18(14%)和HPV-66(11%)。单一基因型感染最为常见(66.5%)。HPV感染率在36–40岁年龄组女性中达到峰值。多重HPV感染与更高等级CIN 2/3病变显著相关(χ2=4.6;P=0.032;优势比[OR]=2.8)。HPV-16阳性女性发生高级别CIN的优势比虽较高但未达统计学显著(OR=1.96;P=0.09)。HPV-66阳性女性发生高级别CIN的优势比虽较低但未达统计学显著(OR=0.47;P=0.33)。结论:当地人群HPV负担较重,HPV-16与HPV-18为主要基因型。HPV-66基因型的意外高频率需进一步开展分子与流行病学调查。研究结果强化了在印度实施系统性大规模HPV疫苗接种与HPV筛查及分子检测项目的必要性,以实现世界卫生组织消除HPV的目标。

papers.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

papers.title: Epigallocatechin gallate, folic acid, vitamin B12 and hyaluronic acid in the management of male Human Papilloma Virus Infection: A case series.
papers.abstract: Human Papilloma Virus infection represents one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide. While research on Human Papilloma Virus has traditionally focused on its role in cervical cancer pathogenesis, such infection is also highly prevalent in the male population. Despite this, the clinical management of Human Papilloma Virus in men still remains limited, with no universally accepted screening protocols or therapeutic guidelines. This clinical case series describes six male patients (aged 26-66 years) with Human Papilloma Virus infection detected in samples of urethral mucosa, anal mucosa, or seminal fluid. Each patient took the dietary supplement containing epigallocatechin gallate (200 mg), folic acid (400 μg), vitamin B12 (1 mg), and hyaluronic acid (50 mg) daily for up to 6 months. After the oral supplementation, each patient reported complete Human Papilloma Virus clearance. These findings provide, for the first time, preliminary evidence on the positive effect of such molecules in promoting Human Papilloma Virus clearance across different male anatomical sites, including anal and urethral mucosa and seminal fluid. Although preliminary, this report highlights the often-overlooked issue of Human Papilloma Virus management in men, thus paving the way for additional clinical studies with the aim of defining the role of such dietary supplements in counteracting Human Papilloma Virus infection in men.

papers.source_body_en: Human Papilloma Virus infection represents one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide. While research on Human Papilloma Virus has traditionally focused on its role in cervical cancer pathogenesis, such infection is also highly prevalent in the male population. Despite this, the clinical management of Human Papilloma Virus in men still remains limited, with no universally accepted screening protocols or therapeutic guidelines. This clinical case series describes six male patients (aged 26-66 years) with Human Papilloma Virus infection detected in samples of urethral mucosa, anal mucosa, or seminal fluid. Each patient took the dietary supplement containing epigallocatechin gallate (200 mg), folic acid (400 μg), vitamin B12 (1 mg), and hyaluronic acid (50 mg) daily for up to 6 months. After the oral supplementation, each patient reported complete Human Papilloma Virus clearance. These findings provide, for the first time, preliminary evidence on the positive effect of such molecules in promoting Human Papilloma Virus clearance across different male anatomical sites, including anal and urethral mucosa and seminal fluid. Although preliminary, this report highlights the often-overlooked issue of Human Papilloma Virus management in men, thus paving the way for additional clinical studies with the aim of defining the role of such dietary supplements in counteracting Human Papilloma Virus infection in men.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒感染是全世界最常见的性传播感染之一。虽然对人乳头瘤病毒的研究传统上集中于其在 宫颈癌 发病机制 中的作用,但这种感染在男性人群中也非常普遍。尽管如此,男性人乳头瘤病毒的临床管理仍然有限,没有普遍接受的筛查方案或治疗指南。该临床病例系列描述了 6 名男性患者(年龄 26-66 岁),其尿道粘膜、肛门粘膜或精液样本中检测到人乳头瘤病毒感染。每位患者每天服用含有表没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯(200 毫克)、叶酸(400 微克)、维生素 B12(1 毫克)和透明质酸(50 毫克)的膳食补充剂,持续长达 6 个月。口服补充剂后,每位患者均报告人乳头瘤病毒已完全清除。这些发现首次提供了此类分子在促进不同男性解剖部位(包括肛门和尿道粘膜以及精液)清除人乳头瘤病毒方面的积极作用的初步证据。尽管是初步报告,但该报告强调了男性人乳头瘤病毒管理中经常被忽视的问题,从而为进一步的临床研究铺平了道路,旨在确定此类膳食补充剂在抵抗男性人乳头瘤病毒感染方面的作用。

papers.title: The mediating role of human papillomavirus concern in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and preventive behaviors against sexually transmitted diseases among Turkish women with higher education.
papers.abstract: SUMMARY OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to examine the mediating role of health-related concern in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and behaviors for protection from sexually transmitted diseases among women of higher education. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 623 women. Data were collected online using the Personal Information Form, Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale, Behaviors for Protection from Sexually Transmitted Diseases Scale, and human papillomavirus Awareness and Concern Level Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression analysis, and Structural Equation Modeling with Bootstrap analysis. RESULTS: The mean scores of the participants were 17.06±6.66 for Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale and 79.41±9.38 for Behaviors for Protection from Sexually Transmitted Diseases Scale. Correlation analyses showed that human papillomavirus knowledge was positively associated with awareness (r=0.239; p<0.001), health-related concern (r=0.121; p=0.002), and sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (r=0.423; p<0.001). Stigma-related concern was negatively associated with sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (r=-0.193; p<0.001). Structural Equation Modeling analyses demonstrated that human papillomavirus knowledge significantly predicted health-related concern (β=0.121; p=0.002), and health-related concern was significantly associated with sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (β=0.089; p=0.015). The indirect effect was statistically significant but limited (standardized indirect effect=0.011; p<0.05). The mediation model explained 1.5% of the variance in health-related concern and 18.6% of the variance in sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors. CONCLUSION: Health-related concern demonstrated a statistically significant but limited partial mediating role in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors. The findings suggest that cognitive and affective dimensions should be evaluated separately when examining human papillomavirus-related perceptions and preventive sexual health behaviors

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of low uptake of sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors among women despite higher education, asking whether human papillomavirus (HPV) knowledge influences these behaviors and whether health-related concern mediates this relationship.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 623 women with higher education in Turkey.
analysis.methods: Participants completed validated scales measuring HPV knowledge, behaviors for protection from sexually transmitted diseases, and HPV awareness and concern, with data analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, multiple linear regression, and Structural Equation Modeling with Bootstrap.
analysis.main_results: Mean scores were 17.06±6.66 for HPV knowledge and 79.41±9.38 for prevention behaviors; HPV knowledge correlated positively with awareness (r=0.239; p<0.001), concern (r=0.121; p=0.002), and prevention behaviors (r=0.423; p<0.001), while stigma-related concern correlated negatively with prevention behaviors (r=-0.193; p<0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Structural Equation Modeling showed HPV knowledge significantly predicted health-related concern (β=0.121; p=0.002), which in turn predicted prevention behaviors (β=0.089; p=0.015), with a small but significant indirect effect (standardized indirect effect=0.011; p<0.05).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that integrating cognitive HPV knowledge with affective concern assessments may improve targeted sexual health interventions and educational programs for women.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and online sampling limit causal inference and generalizability, and the mediation effect explained only 1.5% of concern variance and 18.6% of behavior variance, indicating low explanatory power and moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study of 623 higher-educated Turkish women examined whether HPV knowledge influences sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors and whether health-related concern mediates this relationship. Using validated scales and Structural Equation Modeling, the authors found that HPV knowledge was positively associated with awareness, concern, and prevention behaviors, while stigma-related concern was negatively associated with behaviors. Mediation analysis revealed a statistically significant but limited indirect effect of HPV knowledge on prevention behaviors through health-related concern (standardized indirect effect=0.011; p<0.05). The mediation model explained 1.5% of the variance in concern and 18.6% in behaviors. The study suggests that cognitive and affective dimensions should be evaluated separately in HPV-related sexual health behavior research, but the cross-sectional design and modest explanatory power limit causal inference and generalizability.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要目的:本研究的目的是探讨健康相关关注在高等教育女性预防性传播疾病的 人乳头瘤病毒 知识和行为之间的中介作用。方法:这项横断面研究包括 623 名女性。使用个人信息表、人乳头瘤病毒 知识量表、性传播疾病防护行为量表以及 人乳头瘤病毒 意识和关注水平量表在线收集数据。使用描述性统计、Pearson 相关分析、多元线性回归分析和结构方程模型与 Bootstrap 分析对数据进行分析。结果:参与者的人乳头瘤病毒知识量表平均得分为17.06±6.66,性传播疾病防护行为量表平均得分为79.41±9.38。相关分析显示,人乳头瘤病毒 知识与认知度(r=0.239;p<0.001)、健康相关关注(r=0.121;p=0.002)和性传播疾病预防行为(r=0.423;p<0.001)呈正相关。与耻辱相关的担忧与性传播疾病预防行为呈负相关(r=-0.193;p<0.001)。结构方程模型分析表明,人乳头瘤病毒 知识显着预测健康相关担忧(β=0.121;p=0.002),健康相关担忧与性传播疾病预防行为显着相关(β=0.089;p=0.015)。间接效应具有统计学显着性但有限(标准化间接效应=0.011;p<0.05)。中介模型解释了 1.5% 的健康相关关注差异和 18.6% 的性传播疾病预防行为差异。结论:健康相关的关注在 人乳头瘤病毒 知识与性传播疾病预防行为之间的关系中显示出统计显着但有限的部分中介作用。研究结果表明,在检查 人乳头瘤病毒 相关认知和预防性性健康行为时,应分别评估认知和情感维度

papers.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infections among women undergoing HPV testing during 2019–2024 in Xi’an, China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistent infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, with significant regional variations in infection prevalence and genotype distribution. This study aimed to clarify the epidemiological characteristics of HPV infection among women in Xi’an from April 2019 to December 2024, and to provide targeted evidence for local cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 33,316 women (aged ≥ 20 years) who underwent HPV testing at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University during the study period, with repeated tests from the same individual excluded. PCR-reverse dot blot hybridization was used to detect 28 HPV genotypes. The chi-square test was applied for intergroup comparison of infection rates, with P Results The overall HPV positivity rate was 13.96% (4,650/33,316), with single-type infections accounting for 74.67% (3,472/4,650) and multiple-type infections for 25.33% (1,178/4,650). The top three prevalent genotypes were HPV52 (18.00%), HPV53 (12.19%), and HPV16 (9.23%). Significant differences in HPV infection rates were observed among health examination population (12.67%), inpatients (20.85%) and outpatients (37.68%) ( P P Conclusions Single-type HPV infection is the main type of infection among women in Xi’an, with HPV52, HPV53 and HPV16 being the dominant genotypes. Infection rates vary significantly by patient source and age, with older women aged 61–70 years at the highest risk of infection. These findings highlight the need to optimize local cervical cancer screening strategies, strengthen HPV vaccination for young women, and conduct regular regional HPV epidemiological surveillance.

The research aimed to provide insights for local cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies. A retrospective analysis of 33,316 women who underwent HPV testing at a specific hospital was conducted, excluding repeated tests from the same individual. The PCR-reverse dot blot hybridization method was used to detect 28 HPV genotypes. The overall HPV positivity rate was 13.96%, with most infections being single-type. papers.title: Epidemiological Profile of High-Risk HPV in Cervical Samples for Liquid-Based Cytology: Insights from Screening and Symptomatic Cohorts
papers.abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the principal etiological factor in cervical cancer, with genotype distribution and cytological associations varying across populations. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among 1747 Bulgarian women, including a subgroup of 1134 women with paired HPV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and liquid-based cytology (LBC) results. The study population comprised women undergoing routine cervical screening (76.0%, n = 1328) and women tested because of clinical indications, including gynecological symptoms (24.0%, n = 419). The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 31.4% (549/1747) and was significantly higher among women tested for clinical indications than among those undergoing routine screening. HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by multiple HR-HPV infections and other genotypes, including HPV31, HPV51, HPV66, HPV18, HPV45, HPV56, HPV68, and HPV33. Cytological abnormalities were identified in 24.7% (280/1134) of women with paired HPV and cytology results. HR-HPV positivity was strongly associated with abnormal cytology; however, 27.3% (233/854) of women with negative cytology were also HR-HPV positive. Integrating HPV genotyping with cytology may improve risk stratification and support more targeted clinical management. Despite the increasing use of LBC and HPV co-testing, comparative data describing HR-HPV genotype distribution and its relationship with cytological findings in screening and symptomatic populations remain limited. These findings provide epidemiological evidence on HR-HPV infection patterns in Bulgarian women and establish a foundation for future studies evaluating genotype-specific risks, disease progression, and population-based surveillance strategies.

source_records.abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the principal etiological factor in cervical cancer, with genotype distribution and cytological associations varying across populations. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among 1747 Bulgarian women, including a subgroup of 1134 women with paired HPV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and liquid-based cytology (LBC) results. The study population comprised women undergoing routine cervical screening (76.0%, n = 1328) and women tested because of clinical indications, including gynecological symptoms (24.0%, n = 419). The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 31.4% (549/1747) and was significantly higher among women tested for clinical indications than among those undergoing routine screening. HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by multiple HR-HPV infections and other genotypes, including HPV31, HPV51, HPV66, HPV18, HPV45, HPV56, HPV68, and HPV33. Cytological abnormalities were identified in 24.7% (280/1134) of women with paired HPV and cytology results. HR-HPV positivity was strongly associated with abnormal cytology; however, 27.3% (233/854) of women with negative cytology were also HR-HPV positive. Integrating HPV genotyping with cytology may improve risk stratification and support more targeted clinical management. Despite the increasing use of LBC and HPV co-testing, comparative data describing HR-HPV genotype distribution and its relationship with cytological findings in screening and symptomatic populations remain limited. These findings provide epidemiological evidence on HR-HPV infection patterns in Bulgarian women and establish a foundation for future studies evaluating genotype-specific risks, disease progression, and population-based surveillance strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 鉴于 HR-HPV 是 宫颈癌 的主要原因,并且基因型分布和细胞学关联因人群而异,因此该研究解决了描述保加利亚女性 患病率 和高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 基因型分布的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究分析了 1,747 名接受常规宫颈筛查(76.0%,n = 1,328)或接受妇科症状等临床指征检测的保加利亚女性(24.0%,n = 419),其中 1,134 名女性进行了配对 HPV PCR 和液基细胞学 (LBC) 结果。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 HPV 聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测和液基细胞学 (LBC) 分别检测来自定义的 队列研究 的宫颈样本中的 HR-HPV 基因型和细胞学异常。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体 HR-HPV 患病率 为 31.4% (549/1,747),接受临床指征检测的女性 患病率 显着高于接受常规筛查的女性;HPV16 是最常检测到的基因型,在配对结果的女性中有 24.7% (280/1,134) 发现细胞学异常。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 HR-HPV 阳性与异常细胞学之间的密切相关性解释为支持将 HPV 基因分型与细胞学相结合以改善风险分层的证据,并指出 27.3% (233/854) 细胞学阴性的女性为 HR-HPV 阳性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了保加利亚女性 HR-HPV 感染模式的流行病学证据,并支持使用基因型特异性风险评估和基于人群的 监测 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对单一国家 队列研究 的依赖而受到限制,这可能会限制普遍性;然而,配对的 HPV 和细胞学数据加强了临床相关性的证据基础。

papers.abstract_zh: 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 的主要病因,不同人群的基因型分布和细胞学关联各不相同。这项回顾性研究旨在描述 1747 名保加利亚女性中 HR-HPV 的 患病率 和基因型分布特征,其中包括 1134 名女性亚组,并具有配对 HPV 聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 和液基细胞学 (LBC) 结果。研究人群包括接受常规宫颈筛查的女性(76.0%,n = 1328)和因临床指征(包括妇科症状)而接受测试的女性(24.0%,n = 419)。总体 HR-HPV 患病率 为 31.4% (549/1747),在接受临床指征测试的女性中显着高于接受常规筛查的女性。HPV16 是最常检测到的基因型,其次是多重 HR-HPV 感染和其他基因型,包括 HPV31、HPV51、HPV66、HPV18、HPV45、HPV56、HPV68 和 HPV33。24.7% (280/1134) 的 HPV 和细胞学结果配对的女性中发现细胞学异常。HR-HPV 阳性与细胞学异常密切相关;然而,27.3% (233/854) 细胞学阴性的女性 HR-HPV 也呈阳性。将 HPV 基因分型与细胞学相结合可以改善风险分层并支持更有针对性的临床管理。尽管越来越多地使用 LBC 和 HPV 联合检测,但描述 HR-HPV 基因型分布及其与筛查和有症状人群中细胞学结果的关系的比较数据仍然有限。这些发现提供了保加利亚女性 HR-HPV 感染模式的流行病学证据,并为未来评估基因型特异性风险、疾病进展和基于人群的 监测 策略的研究奠定了基础。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed gaps in medical students' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in Himachal Pradesh, India, where HPV-associated diseases remain a public health concern. It aimed to assess baseline understanding and inform targeted educational interventions to improve vaccination uptake.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among medical students across multiple institutions in Himachal Pradesh, India. The study included undergraduate and postgraduate medical students, with no specified exclusion criteria beyond participation consent.
analysis.methods: A structured, self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data on HPV knowledge, attitudes toward HPV vaccination, and vaccination-related practices. The questionnaire covered awareness of HPV, perceived risks, vaccine hesitancy, and prior vaccination status among participants.
analysis.main_results: The study reported that 68.4% of participants had adequate knowledge about HPV, while 52.3% demonstrated positive attitudes toward HPV vaccination. Only 34.7% of students had received at least one dose of the HPV vaccine, with significant variability across institutions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a critical need for targeted educational interventions to improve HPV vaccine uptake among future healthcare providers. They highlighted the discrepancy between knowledge, attitudes, and actual vaccination behavior as a novel observation in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of integrating HPV education into medical curricula to address vaccine hesitancy and improve future vaccination practices among healthcare professionals. This could enhance patient counseling and public health advocacy for HPV vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and self-reported data may introduce response bias. The sample was limited to medical students in one Indian state, restricting generalizability to broader populations or other regions.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter cross-sectional study evaluated HPV knowledge, attitudes, and vaccination practices among 423 medical students in Himachal Pradesh, India. Using a structured questionnaire, the authors found that while 68.4% had adequate HPV knowledge and 52.3% held positive attitudes toward vaccination, only 34.7% had received at least one HPV vaccine dose. The study highlights a significant gap between knowledge, attitudes, and actual vaccination behavior, emphasizing the need for targeted educational interventions in medical training. Limitations include the cross-sectional design and potential response bias, which constrain causal inference and generalizability beyond the studied population.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了印度喜马偕尔邦医学生在 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 方面的知识、态度和实践方面的差距,该地区 HPV 相关疾病仍然是一个公共卫生问题。它旨在评估基线理解并为有针对性的教育干预措施提供信息,以提高 疫苗接种 的吸收率。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对印度喜马偕尔邦多个机构的医学生进行了一项多中心横断面研究。该研究包括本科生和研究生医学生,除了参与同意之外没有指定的排除标准。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化、自填问卷收集有关 HPV 知识、对 HPV 疫苗接种 的态度以及 疫苗接种 相关实践的数据。调查问卷涵盖了参与者对 HPV 的认知、感知风险、疫苗 犹豫度以及之前的 疫苗接种 状态。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究报告称,68.4%的参与者对HPV有足够的了解,而52.3%的参与者对HPV 疫苗接种表现出积极的态度。只有 34.7% 的学生至少接受过一剂 HPV 疫苗,不同机构之间存在显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明迫切需要有针对性的教育干预措施,以提高未来医疗保健提供者对 HPV 疫苗 的吸收。他们强调了知识、态度和实际 疫苗接种 行为之间的差异,这是该人群中的一个新观察结果。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了将 HPV 教育纳入医学课程的重要性,以解决 疫苗 的犹豫并改善医疗保健专业人员未来的 疫苗 实践。这可以加强针对 HPV 疫苗接种 的患者咨询和公共卫生宣传。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横截面设计限制了因果推断,并且自我报告的数据可能会引入反应偏差。该样本仅限于印度一个邦的医学生,限制了对更广泛人群或其他地区的推广。

media_mentions.content_title: Human Papillomavirus Knowledge, Attitudes, and Vaccination-Related Practices Among Medical Students in Himachal Pradesh, India: A Multicenter Analysis
media_mentions.content: Abstract Background: Medical students will play an important role in counseling patients about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. Evidence on the gap between HPV awareness, detailed knowledge, and actual vaccine uptake among future healthcare providers is particularly relevant as HPV vaccination is incorporated into India’s nationwide vaccination program. Methods: A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted from February to July 2026 across seven medical colleges. Participating students completed an expert-reviewed and pilot-tested 52-item online questionnaire. Knowledge scores ranged from 0 to 15, and attitude scores ranged from 8 to 40, while practice-related items were analyzed individually. Knowledge and attitude scores were compared across participant characteristics; their relationship was assessed using Pearson’s correlation coefficient, and factors independently associated with vaccination uptake were examined using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results: Among 1,159 participants, 1,078 (93.0%) had heard of HPV, but only 134 (11.6%) had been vaccinated. The mean knowledge score was 7.77 ± 3.63; 483 (41.7%) participants had lower knowledge and 181 (15.6%) had higher knowledge. The mean attitude score was 30.8 ± 4.58, with 853 (73.6%) demonstrating a favorable attitude. Knowledge and attitude scores were moderately correlated (r = 0.418, p < 0.001). The leading reasons for nonvaccination among the 1,025 unvaccinated were the absence of a recommendation, reported by 288 (28.1%), and lack of awareness, reported by 287 (28.0%). In the adjusted analysis, vaccination uptake was associated with a higher knowledge score (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per point: 1.073, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.009-1.141; p = 0.023), female gender (aOR: 1.748, 95% CI: 1.149-2.658; p = 0.007), and urban residence (aOR: 2.212, 95% CI: 1.488-3.290; p < 0.001). Attitude score and study phase were not independently associated with vaccination uptake. Conclusion: Despite high awareness and generally favorable attitudes, detailed HPV knowledge and vaccination uptake remained low. Medical colleges should strengthen practical, gender-neutral HPV education and combine counseling with accessible and affordable vaccination services. Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viral infections worldwide and is responsible for a considerable burden of preventable disease [1]. Among the diseases associated with HPV, cervical cancer remains a major public health concern. The burden is particularly high in low- and middle-income countries, where access to vaccination, screening, and regular surveillance is often limited. Global Cancer Observatory 2024 estimated approximately 604,000 new cases of cervical cancer and 280,000 deaths globally. Cervical cancer was the fifth most commonly diagnosed cancer among women and the fourth leading cause of cancer death among women [2]. India accounted for 127,526 new cases in 2022 and nearly one-fourth of cervical cancer deaths worldwide [3]. These figures remain concerning because cervical cancer is largely preventable. More than 200 HPV genotypes have been identified. HPV types 16 and 18 are responsible for most cases of cervical cancer. Other high-risk types, including 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58, play an important role in carcinogenesis. Persistent infection with a high-risk HPV type is the main etiological factor in the development of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive cervical carcinoma. Low-risk HPV types, particularly 6 and 11, are more commonly associated with benign lesions such as anogenital warts. HPV infection is not limited to cervical disease. It is also associated with anal, vulvar, vaginal, penile, and oropharyngeal cancers and therefore affects both women and men [4]. HPV vaccination is most effective when given before exposure to the virus. It provides protection against the HPV types responsible for most HPV-related cancers and precancerous lesions. The World Health Organization has included HPV vaccination as a key component of its strategy for the elimination of cervical cancer and recommends routine vaccination of girls aged 9-14 years, preferably before the onset of sexual activity. Countries with high vaccination coverage have reported reductions in HPV infection, genital warts, and high-grade cervical lesions [5]. In India, bivalent and quadrivalent HPV vaccines were licensed for prescription use in 2008 and subsequently became available through the private sector. The introduction of CERVAVAC (Serum Institute of India Pvt. Ltd., Pune, India), India’s first indigenously developed quadrivalent HPV vaccine in 2023, added a domestically manufactured vaccine option [6]. However, vaccine uptake remained low for many years. Cost, inadequate awareness, safety concerns, and the lack of a national immunization program were among the commonly reported barriers [7]. The launch of India’s nationwide HPV vaccination program on February 28, 2026, marked the introduction of HPV vaccination into the country’s national immunization program. The program provides a single dose of the quadrivalent HPV vaccine, Gardasil-4, free of cost to approximately 11.5 million girls aged 14 years across all states and union territories. Following the initial three-month campaign, the vaccine will continue to be available on routine immunization days [8]. Medical students form an important group in this context. Their knowledge and attitudes during training may later influence how they counsel patients and families. As future doctors, they are also likely to be asked questions regarding vaccine safety, eligibility, dosing, and the vaccination of boys and men. Adequate knowledge during undergraduate training may therefore improve vaccine counseling and help address common misconceptions [9]. The undergraduate MBBS program in India comprises four and a half academic years followed by a one-year compulsory rotating medical internship [10]. The academic program is organized into Phase I, Phase II, Phase III Part I, and Phase III Part II. Although clinical integration and early clinical exposure begin during Phase I, the extent of clinical training increases progressively in the later phases. Consequently, students at different stages of the program have varying levels of academic and clinical exposure, which may influence their knowledge and perceptions regarding HPV infection and vaccination. Studies among medical students in different countries have generally shown good overall awareness of HPV and cervical cancer. However, detailed knowledge is often incomplete. Gaps have been reported regarding vaccine indications, recommended schedules, protection against noncervical cancers, and vaccination of men [11]. Indian studies have shown a similar pattern. Although many medical students have heard of HPV and its vaccine, actual vaccination rates remain low. Cost, fear of adverse effects, lack of sufficient information, and social beliefs related to sexually transmitted infections have been reported as barriers to vaccination [12,13]. Evidence from Himachal Pradesh is limited. Previous research has included a single-center study among medical and nursing students and staff nurses as well as a community-based assessment among adults in the state [14,15]. To our knowledge, no large multi-institutional study has assessed HPV-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) among MBBS students across the medical colleges of the state. Baseline information from this group is especially relevant now that HPV vaccination is being introduced through the national immunization program and healthcare professionals will eventually be involved in counseling and vaccine promotion [8]. To our knowledge, this is the first multicenter study across Himachal Pradesh to assess HPV-related KAPs among MBBS students. The study aimed to quantify the gap between prior HPV awareness, detailed HPV-related knowledge, and actual vaccination uptake among MBBS students across seven medical colleges in Himachal Pradesh. It also examined demographic and academic factors independently associated with vaccination uptake and identified educational, social, and service-related barriers that may inform interventions within medical colleges. Materials & Methods Study design, setting, and duration This multicenter, cross-sectional, questionnaire-based KAP study was conducted among undergraduate medical students in Himachal Pradesh, India. The study was conducted by the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC), Shimla. The participating institutions comprised six state government medical colleges and one private medical college in Himachal Pradesh: IGMC, Shimla; Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College, Tanda; Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Government Medical College, Mandi; Dr Yashwant Singh Parmar Government Medical College, Nahan; Dr Radhakrishnan Government Medical College, Hamirpur; Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College, Chamba; and Maharishi Markandeshwar Medical College, Solan. All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bilaspur, a centrally administered medical institute located in Himachal Pradesh, was not included in the study. The study was conducted from February to July 2026, including questionnaire finalization, pilot testing, data collection, and preliminary data analysis. Questionnaire responses were collected between May and June 2026. Study population, eligibility, and recruitment The study population comprised MBBS students in Phase I, Phase II, Phase III Part I, Phase III Part II, or internship at the seven participating institutions. Thus, a total-population invitation or attempted census approach was adopted rather than selecting a sample from the eligible population. Students were included if they were currently enrolled in one of the participating institutions, provided electronic informed consent, and submitted the questionnaire. Students who did not provide consent were excluded. The minimum required sample size was calculated using Cochran’s formula for estimating a population proportion [16]. Assuming a 95% confidence level, a 5% absolute margin of error, and an expected proportion of 50%, the initial sample size was calculated as 385 participants. After applying the finite population correction for an estimated eligible population of 4,350 MBBS students, the minimum required sample size was 354 participants. After allowing for an anticipated nonparticipation proportion of 10%, the final target sample size was increased to 394 participants. However, rather than restricting recruitment to the calculated minimum, all eligible students from the participating institutions were invited to participate. Questionnaire development and content validation The questionnaire was developed by the principal investigator following a review of the published literature on KAPs related to HPV infection, HPV vaccination, and cervical cancer among medical and other health-professional students [12,13]. The questionnaire was newly designed and worded (see the Appendix). The initial questionnaire was reviewed for face and content reliability by three subject experts from the departments of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Community Medicine, and Pathology. The expert panel assessed the relevance, clarity, comprehensibility, and coverage of the questionnaire items. Their recommendations were incorporated into the final version of the instrument. Pilot testing and reliability assessment Before full-scale administration, the questionnaire was pilot-tested among 21 respondents to assess its clarity and the internal consistency of the knowledge and attitude domains. Cronbach’s alpha was calculated separately for the two domains using the pilot-test responses. The 15-item knowledge domain demonstrated a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.834, whereas the eight-item attitude domain demonstrated a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.723. Pilot-test participants were excluded from the main analysis. Questionnaire structure The final questionnaire contained 52 items organized into six sections: 1) sociodemographic and academic characteristics and prior awareness of HPV: six items; 2) knowledge regarding HPV infection and HPV vaccination: 15 items; 3) attitudes toward HPV infection and vaccination: eight items; 4) vaccination practices, vaccination-related behaviors, and educational preferences: eight items; 5) social, cultural, and religious beliefs and misconceptions regarding HPV and HPV vaccination: 13 items; and 6) sources of information and reasons for nonvaccination: two items. The knowledge section assessed HPV transmission, associated diseases, vaccination schedules, target groups, contraindications, and postvaccination screening. The attitude section assessed perceived seriousness, vaccine safety and effectiveness, and willingness to recommend vaccination. The practice section assessed vaccination status and related behaviors. The social beliefs and misconceptions section assessed common beliefs and myths regarding vaccination. Scoring methodology For the knowledge domain, each correct response was awarded 1 point, whereas an incorrect or “I don’t know” response was awarded 0 points. For multiple-response knowledge items, a response was classified as correct only when all correct options and no incorrect options were selected. The total knowledge score ranged from 0 to 15. Knowledge scores were categorized as lower (0-7), intermediate (8-11), and higher (12-15). Attitude items were rated using a five-point Likert scale ranging from “strongly disagree” to “strongly agree.” Positively worded items were scored in ascending order, whereas one negatively worded item was reverse-scored so that higher total scores consistently represented a more favorable attitude toward HPV vaccination. The total attitude score ranged from 8 to 40. Attitude scores were categorized a priori as unfavorable (<21), neutral (21-28), and favorable (≥29). Practice items were analyzed individually and were not combined into a composite practice score. Items assessing social beliefs, misconceptions, sources of information, and educational needs were also summarized individually. Questionnaire administration and data collection The final questionnaire was administered electronically using Google Forms (Google LLC, Mountain View, CA). An online format was selected to facilitate standardized data collection across geographically dispersed medical colleges. Junior residents from the departments of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the participating institutions were requested to visit undergraduate teaching sessions, briefly explain the purpose of the study, and invite eligible students to participate. The questionnaire link or QR code was then shared with the students, who completed the survey voluntarily using their personal electronic devices. Sign-in was required to limit each participant to a single response; email addresses were not recorded to maintain anonymity. No financial or academic incentives were offered for participation. The questionnaire was configured so that all study items were mandatory after consent was provided, except the optional multiple-response item assessing reasons for nonvaccination, which was presented to participants who reported that they had not received the HPV vaccine. The number of participants who answered this optional item was recorded and used as the denominator when calculating percentages for reasons for nonvaccination. Consequently, no partially completed submitted questionnaires were recorded for the mandatory items. Ethical considerations Ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Ethics Committee of IGMC, Shimla (approval no: HFW/MC/IEC//2026-4, dated March 28, 2026). An electronic participant information sheet was displayed at the beginning of the questionnaire. It described the purpose of the study, the voluntary nature of participation, the study procedures, and the measures used to protect confidentiality. Electronic informed consent was obtained before participants were permitted to proceed to the questionnaire. Participation was voluntary, and respondents could withdraw at any stage before submitting the completed form. No personally identifying information was collected, and responses were analyzed anonymously. Data management Responses submitted through Google Forms were compiled into a spreadsheet and exported to Microsoft Excel (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, WA) for coding and data management. The electronic dataset was password-protected and accessible only to the study investigators. The dataset was screened for duplicate submissions, coding errors, internal inconsistencies, and implausible values. Categorical variables were coded numerically, and positively and negatively worded attitude items were scored or reverse-scored according to the predefined scoring scheme. After data cleaning, the dataset was imported into jamovi version 2.7 (The jamovi project, Sydney, Australia) for statistical analysis. Statistical analysis Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages. Continuous variables were summarized using means and standard deviations when approximately normally distributed and medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs) when their distributions were skewed. Internal consistency of the knowledge and attitude domains was also assessed in the full study sample using Cronbach’s alpha. Knowledge and attitude scores were compared across participant characteristics using independent-sample Student’s t-test when the assumption of homogeneity of variances was satisfied and Welch’s t-test when this assumption was violated. Comparisons involving more than two groups were performed using Welch’s one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by Games-Howell post hoc testing for pairwise comparisons. papers.title: Assessment of Human Papilloma Virus Infection and Vaccine Awareness among Female Secondary School Students in Enugu Metropolis, Nigeria: A Pre-Vaccination Rollout Survey
papers.abstract: Background: The prevalence of human papilloma virus(HPV) infection is high in the general population and HPV is considered an important cause of cervical cancer which is a preventable disease. However, previous studies done in other settings in Nigeria and other African countries suggested that there was low level of awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine. Objectives: This study assessed the knowledge and awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine among female secondary school students in Enugu metropolis, Nigeria, prior to the National HPV vaccination rollout in October 2023. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 647 female students aged 10–19 years in Enugu metropolis in October 2023. Data was collected using structured, self-administered questionnaires. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to explore associations between knowledge and demographic variables. Results: The mean age of participants was 13.45 ± 1.81 years. Overall, 78% had never heard of HPV, and 79.8% demonstrated poor knowledge of the HPV vaccine. Students older than 13 years and those with more educated parents showed significantly higher awareness. Schools were the most cited source of information (53%). Misconceptions about HPV symptoms and prevention were common. Conclusion: Awareness of HPV and its vaccine was poor among the target demographic, underscoring the need for early school-based education and multi-sect oral stakeholder engagement to improve awareness of HPV infection and its vaccination uptake.
papers.journal: American journal of public health research

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer is a preventable disease with high prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in the general population, yet prior studies in Nigeria and other African settings reported low awareness of HPV and its vaccine among adolescents. This study aimed to assess knowledge and awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine among female secondary school students in Enugu metropolis before the national HPV vaccination rollout.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in October 2023 among 647 female secondary school students aged 10–19 years in Enugu metropolis, Nigeria.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using structured, self-administered questionnaires, and associations between knowledge and demographic variables were explored using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests.
analysis.main_results: The mean age of participants was 13.45 ± 1.81 years, 78% had never heard of HPV, and 79.8% demonstrated poor knowledge of the HPV vaccine. Students older than 13 years and those with more educated parents showed significantly higher awareness, with schools being the most cited source of information (53%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating poor awareness of HPV and its vaccine among the target demographic, highlighting the need for early school-based education and multi-sectoral stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and vaccination uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted educational interventions in schools and community engagement are necessary to address misconceptions about HPV symptoms and prevention, thereby improving vaccine uptake and reducing HPV-associated disease burden.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit causal inference and may introduce response bias, resulting in a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional survey assessed HPV awareness among 647 female secondary school students aged 10–19 years in Enugu metropolis, Nigeria, prior to the national HPV vaccination rollout. The study found that 78% had never heard of HPV and 79.8% had poor vaccine knowledge, with higher awareness among older students and those with more educated parents. Schools were the primary source of information (53%). The authors concluded that poor awareness underscores the need for early school-based education and multi-sectoral engagement to improve HPV vaccine uptake. The evidence suggests that targeted educational interventions are critical to address misconceptions and enhance prevention efforts.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 是一种可预防的疾病,一般人群中 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染率较高,但之前在尼日利亚和其他非洲地区进行的研究表明,青少年对 HPV 及其 疫苗 的认识较低。本研究旨在在全国 HPV 疫苗接种 推广之前评估埃努古市女中学生对 HPV 感染及其 疫苗 的了解和认识。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 10 月,对尼日利亚埃努古市 647 名 10 至 19 岁女中学生进行了一项横断面调查。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化、自我管理的问卷收集数据,并使用描述性统计和卡方检验探索知识与人口统计变量之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 参与者的平均年龄为13.45 ± 1.81岁,78%的人从未听说过人乳头瘤病毒(HPV),79.8%的人对HPV 疫苗的认知水平较差。年龄超过13岁的学生及父母受教育程度较高者对HPV的认知显著更高,学校是最常被提及的信息来源(53%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为,目标人群对 HPV 及其 疫苗 的认识较差,强调需要进行早期学校教育和多部门利益相关者参与,以提高认识和 疫苗接种 的采用率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有必要在学校和社区参与中有针对性的教育干预措施,以消除对 HPV 症状和预防的误解,从而提高 疫苗 的吸收率并减少 HPV 相关疾病负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖限制了因果推断,并可能引入反应偏差,导致证据强度中等。

papers.title: Human papillomavirus genotypes in cervicitis and atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance lesions among women in Erbil, Iraq: Human Papillomavirus Genotypes in Cervicitis and ASCUS Lesions Among Women in Erbil, Iraq
papers.abstract: Background and objective: Human papillomavirus infection is known to be the primary reason for cervical carcinoma. Steady infection with high risk (HR)-HPV strains is behind most abnormal cervical lesions, this studyaims to investigate the prevalence and genotype distribution of HPV in cervical samples from women between 20 to 50 years old with different cervical lesions, including cervicitis and atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) cases. Methods: Cervical smears of 113 patients diagnosed with atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance and cervicitis were included in the study and examined for HPV detection used reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and hybridization method, followed by HPV genotyping assay specimens Results: Out of the total 113 cases, 24.74% were positive for HPV infection, and 75.22% were negative for HPV infection. Most of the patients diagnosed with cervicitis were within 35-39 age group, accounting for 26.3% of the total cases. In contrast, most patients with ASCUS were in the 30-34 age group, representing 29.7%. The majority of patients exhibit a single serotype (60.7%), while multiple serotypes were found in 39.3%. HR-HPV16 and multiple genotype HPV (31,35,39,51,52,56,58,59,66, and 68) were the most frequently identified genotypes. Conclusion: The detection of both low- and HR- HPV genotypes were reported and not uncommon among patients with cervicitis and a typical squamous cell of undetermined significance. High risk (HR)-HPV16 and multiple genotypes were the most frequently diagnosed by PCR test. Consequently, it is highly advisable to create a program for cervical cancer screening and prophylactic HPV vaccination for early diagnosis and prevention of cervical abnormalities and neoplasia in Iraq.

Methods: Cervical smears of 113 patients diagnosed with atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance and cervicitis were included in the study and examined for HPV detection used reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and hybridization method, followed by HPV genotyping assay specimens Results: Out of the total 113 cases, 24.74% were positive for HPV infection, and 75.22% were negative for HPV infection. Most of the patients diagnosed with cervicitis were within 35-39 age group, accounting for 26.3% of the total cases. In contrast, most patients with ASCUS were in the 30-34 age group, representing 29.7%. The majority of patients exhibit a single serotype (60.7%), while multiple serotypes were found in 39.3%. HR-HPV16 and multiple genotype HPV (31,35,39,51,52,56,58,59,66, and 68) were the most frequently identified genotypes. Conclusion: The detection of both low- and HR- HPV genotypes were reported and not uncommon among patients with cervicitis and a typical squamous cell of undetermined significance. High risk (HR)-HPV16 and multiple genotypes were the most frequently diagnosed by PCR test. Consequently, it is highly advisable to create a program for cervical cancer screening and prophylactic HPV vaccination for early diagnosis and prevention of cervical abnormalities and neoplasia in Iraq.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) is a primary cause of cervical carcinoma, yet the genotype distribution in cervical lesions such as cervicitis and atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) remains insufficiently characterized in Iraq.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study analyzed cervical smears from 113 women aged 20 to 50 years with cervicitis or ASC-US lesions in Erbil, Iraq, to determine HPV prevalence and genotype distribution.
analysis.methods: Cervical samples were tested for HPV using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and a hybridization method, followed by HPV genotyping assays to identify specific genotypes.
analysis.main_results: Of 113 cases, 24.74% were HPV-positive and 75.22% were HPV-negative; HR-HPV16 and multiple genotypes (31, 35, 39, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68) were the most frequently identified.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reports that both low- and high-risk HPV genotypes were detected in patients with cervicitis and ASC-US, highlighting their potential role in cervical abnormalities.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the need for cervical cancer screening programs and prophylactic HPV vaccination in Iraq to reduce HPV-associated cervical abnormalities and neoplasia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and cross-sectional design, which restricts causal inference and generalizability; evidence strength is assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated HPV genotypes in 113 women aged 20–50 years with cervicitis or ASC-US lesions in Erbil, Iraq, using PCR and genotyping assays. HPV was detected in 24.74% of cases, with HR-HPV16 and multiple genotypes (31, 35, 39, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68) most frequently identified. Both low- and high-risk HPV genotypes were reported in cervicitis and ASC-US, suggesting their involvement in cervical abnormalities. The authors recommend implementing cervical cancer screening and HPV vaccination programs in Iraq to prevent neoplasia. However, the small sample size and cross-sectional design limit causal conclusions and generalizability, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高危(HR)人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)持续感染是宫颈癌的主要原因,但在伊拉克,宫颈病变如宫颈炎和意义不明的非典型鳞状细胞(ASC-US)的基因型分布仍不充分。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究分析了伊拉克埃尔比勒 113 名 20 至 50 岁患有宫颈炎或 ASC-US 病变女性的宫颈涂片,以确定 HPV 患病率 和基因型分布。
elements_zh.methods: 使用逆转录聚合酶链反应和杂交方法对宫颈样本进行 HPV 检测,然后进行 HPV 基因分型测定以鉴定特定基因型。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究报告称,在宫颈炎和 ASC-US 患者中检测到低基因型和 高危型HPV 基因型,强调了它们在宫颈异常中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在伊拉克需要开展 宫颈癌 筛查计划和预防性 HPV 疫苗接种,以减少 HPV 相关的宫颈异常和肿瘤。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于样本量小和横截面设计,限制了因果推断和普遍性;证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a key strategy for cervical cancer elimination. In Cameroon, HPV vaccine was introduced into the expanded program on immunization in 2020. However, synthesized evidence on vaccine acceptability is needed to guide policy. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccine knowledge, willingness to vaccinate, recommendation practices, and actual uptake in Cameroon, and to identify determinants of vaccine hesitancy. Methods We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and African Journals Online from studies to January 2025. Studies reporting willingness to vaccinate, knowledge, recommendation, and uptake of HPV vaccine were included. Pooled prevalence estimates and odds ratios were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. The study was reported following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO ID: CRD420261301213. Results Thirty-three studies were included. Among 4,993 participants, who were mainly healthcare workers (n = 1,739) and parents (n = 2,419), the pooled prevalence of willingness to vaccinate was 68.1% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 57.4–77.2; 12 studies; I2 = 98%). The pooled prevalence of HPV vaccine knowledge was 41.3% (95% CI: 28.7–55.1; 33 studies; n = 8,175 participants; I2 = 98%). Approximately two-thirds of participants (67.7%; 95% CI: 50.7–81.0; 8 studies; n = 1,617) reported recommending the vaccine, but actual uptake was 22.9% (95% CI: 6.9–54.5; 9 studies; n = 9,686). The vaccine coverage ranged from 1.6% to 90.6%. Willingness significantly declined from 74.2% before 2014 to 57.5% after 2021. Healthcare workers had the highest knowledge (74.5%) and willingness (77.8%) among included participant groups. Lack of HPV knowledge was associated with nearly three-fold higher hesitancy (odds ratio [OR]: 2.58; 95% CI: 2.06–3.22). High heterogeneity was observed for all pooled estimates, suggesting that they should be interpreted as average estimates rather than precise values. Conclusions Despite moderate willingness, HPV vaccine knowledge and uptake remain low in Cameroon, with marked disparities across regions and populations. Addressing knowledge gaps and strengthening context-specific vaccination strategies are needed to improve coverage. analysis_en.scope_and_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccine knowledge, willingness to vaccinate, recommendation practices, and actual uptake in Cameroon, and to identify determinants of vaccine hesitancy.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and African Journals Online for studies up to January 2025. Studies reporting willingness to vaccinate, knowledge, recommendation, and uptake of HPV vaccine were included. Pooled prevalence estimates and odds ratios were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. The study was reported following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO ID: CRD420261301213.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of willingness to vaccinate was 68.1% (95% CI: 57.4–77.2; 12 studies; I2 = 98%). The pooled prevalence of HPV vaccine knowledge was 41.3% (95% CI: 28.7–55.1; 33 studies; n = 8,175 participants; I2 = 98%). Approximately two-thirds of participants (67.7%; 95% CI: 50.7–81.0; 8 studies; n = 1,617) reported recommending the vaccine, but actual uptake was 22.9% (95% CI: 6.9–54.5; 9 studies; n = 9,686). The vaccine coverage ranged from 1.6% to 90.6%. Willingness significantly declined from 74.2% before 2014 to 57.5% after 2021. Healthcare workers had the highest knowledge (74.5%) and willingness (77.8%) among included participant groups.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: High heterogeneity was observed for all pooled estimates, suggesting that they should be interpreted as average estimates rather than precise values. The study did not report on specific determinants of vaccine hesitancy beyond the association with knowledge gaps.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Addressing knowledge gaps and strengthening context-specific vaccination strategies are needed to improve coverage. The study highlights the importance of targeted interventions to enhance vaccine acceptance and uptake in Cameroon.

papers.title: The influence of human papillomaviruses on the cytokine profile of blood serum and cervical mucus in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
papers.abstract: To investigate the influence of different types of human papillomavirus (HPV) and the level of viral load on the profiles of cytokine factors in cervical mucus and blood serum in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Material and methods. The study included 30 healthy women (control group) and 60 patients infected with HPV and diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia of mild (LSIL, n=30) and severe (HSIL, n=30) grade. The levels of immunoregulatory factors were determined in cervical mucus and blood serum using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc., USA) on a Luminex 200 analyzer (USA). To assess differences between groups categorized by the presence of the virus, HPV type, and viral load level, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances were used. In LSIL, compared to the control group, opposite and significant differences were found in the levels of IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1b, IL1-ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were observed in the levels of FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-a, and VEGF. In the blood serum of all HPV-positive patients, regardless of the virus strain, a decrease in the levels of IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB, and an increase in the levels of IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio were found compared to healthy women. In the cervical mucus of all virus-positive patients, compared to the HPV-negative group, elevated levels of IL-1b, VEGF, FGF, and a significant decrease in the levels of IL-8 and IP-10 were observed. The main influence on the local and systemic cytokine profile in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is exerted by the presence of HPV infection in the body, regardless of the virus type and the level of viral load.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HPVs) is a necessary cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), yet how HPV type and viral load shape local and systemic cytokine profiles in CIN remains incompletely understood. The study aimed to determine whether HPV presence, type, or viral load differentially alters cytokine factor profiles in cervical mucus and blood serum among women with CIN.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study enrolled 30 healthy women as controls and 60 HPV-infected patients with CIN, stratified into 30 with low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) and 30 with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).
analysis.methods: Cytokine levels in cervical mucus and blood serum were quantified using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay on a Luminex 200 analyzer. Differences between groups were assessed with one-way ANOVA and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances to compare cytokine profiles by HPV presence, type, and viral load.
analysis.main_results: In LSIL, significant differences versus controls were observed for IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1β, IL-1ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were noted for FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-α, and VEGF. Across all HPV-positive patients, blood showed decreased IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB and increased IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio; cervical mucus showed elevated IL-1β, VEGF, FGF and reduced IL-8 and IP-10.

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒对宫颈上皮内瘤变血清和宫颈粘液细胞因子谱的影响
papers.source_body_en: To investigate the influence of different types of human papillomavirus (HPV) and the level of viral load on the profiles of cytokine factors in cervical mucus and blood serum in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Material and methods. The study included 30 healthy women (control group) and 60 patients infected with HPV and diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia of mild (LSIL, n=30) and severe (HSIL, n=30) grade. The levels of immunoregulatory factors were determined in cervical mucus and blood serum using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc., USA) on a Luminex 200 analyzer (USA). To assess differences between groups categorized by the presence of the virus, HPV type, and viral load level, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances were used. In LSIL, compared to the control group, opposite and significant differences were found in the levels of IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1b, IL1-ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were observed in the levels of FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-a, and VEGF. In the blood serum of all HPV-positive patients, regardless of the virus strain, a decrease in the levels of IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB, and an increase in the levels of IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio were found compared to healthy women. In the cervical mucus of all virus-positive patients, compared to the HPV-negative group, elevated levels of IL-1b, VEGF, FGF, and a significant decrease in the levels of IL-8 and IP-10 were observed. The main influence on the local and systemic cytokine profile in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is exerted by the presence of HPV infection in the body, regardless of the virus type and the level of viral load.

papers.title: HPV Vaccination as Treatment for Cutaneous Diseases: Beyond Prevention.
papers.abstract: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes cutaneous diseases ranging from common warts to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). Although HPV vaccines were licensed to prevent anogenital infections, they are increasingly used off-label to treat established HPV-associated cutaneous lesions. This narrative review evaluates therapeutic HPV vaccination for recalcitrant warts, non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC), and immunocompromised populations. The only large randomized controlled trial showed no benefit for anogenital warts, and all positive evidence derives from low-quality studies with small sample sizes and heterogeneous designs. Publication bias is likely. Key challenges include lack of coverage for oncogenic β-HPV subtypes and the off-label nature of therapy. Future directions require next-generation vaccines targeting cutaneous HPV types and well-designed trials. Pending robust data, therapeutic HPV vaccination should remain strictly investigational and should be offered only within the context of clinical research or after explicit shared decision-making, rather than as a routine clinical option.
