papers.title: Oncoviruses at the Crossroads of Ageing and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms and Key Signalling Pathways.
papers.abstract: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

papers.title_zh: 处于衰老和癌症十字路口的肿瘤病毒:分子机制和关键信号通路。
papers.source_body_en: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.
papers.abstract_zh: 肿瘤病毒是导致大部分人类癌症的原因,并且已成为 宿主 细胞途径的关键调节剂,该途径也控制着衰老。病毒肿瘤发生、衰老和癌症的融合反映了共同的分子机制,包括基因组不稳定性、表观遗传改变、端粒磨损和慢性炎症。越来越多的证据表明,人乳头瘤病毒、Epstein-Barr病毒、乙型和丙型肝炎病毒以及卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒等肿瘤病毒会主动重编程宿主信号网络,以促进持续感染、免疫逃避和恶性转化。这篇综述综合了目前关于肿瘤病毒如何与衰老和癌症的关键特征相交叉的知识,特别强调了桥接这些过程的信号通路。包括 p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-catenin 在内的中央通路经常成为病毒蛋白的目标,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用不仅促进肿瘤发生,而且加速与衰老相关的细胞功能障碍,例如免疫衰老和炎症。此外,我们讨论了病毒诱导的肿瘤微环境调节和 宿主 免疫应答 如何促进衰老与癌症之间的动态相互作用。了解这些相互关联的途径可以为了解肿瘤病毒作为与年龄相关的衰退和癌症发展的驱动因素的双重作用提供有价值的见解。阐明这些机制可能会揭示预防和治疗老龄化人群中与病毒相关的恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。

papers.title: HPV Self-Collection Experience in US Hispanic/Latinx Women Using a Device Designed for at-Home Collection.
papers.abstract: Background Cervical cancer is a preventable disease, and reaching populations who are under-screened and/or at highest risk is essential to the goal of disease elimination. Hispanic women in the US have a disproportionately higher incidence rate than non-Hispanic women. Objective Post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study of the unique experience and preferences among Hispanic compared to non-Hispanic participants with the goal of facilitating and improving screening and follow-up in more vulnerable populations. Methods Women 25 to 65 years who were enrolled performed self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. For method comparison, a clinician-collected (CC) sample was obtained. Participants also completed usability and screening preference surveys. Results A total of 609 participants were consented and 603 used the SC device. Of the 603 SC users, 115 (19.1%) identified themselves as Hispanic/Latinx. Compared to non-Hispanic women, Hispanic women, had significantly lower annual income (p < .001), a lower percentage of private insurance with more uninsured (p < .001) and lower levels of education (p < .001). There was no significant difference between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening. No difference was noted in delaying screening, although English Not Primary speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay (p = 0.22). Financial barriers were observed to be more of an impediment to Hispanic women compared to non-Hispanic women (p = 0.016). Negative experiences with in-clinic speculum exams were similar; however, Hispanic women (78%) expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC than non-Hispanic women (62%), (p = 0.001). Both populations reported that they would be more likely to stay up to date with cervical cancer screening with the at-home SC device, but non-Hispanic women to a significantly lesser degree (p = 0.002). In terms of assessing utility of telemedicine in screening, both populations reported similar engagement in healthcare activities, willingness to try new technology and current use of smartphones. Hispanic and non-Hispanic women were both nearly equally divided as to their preference for in-clinic visits vs telehealth. Conclusions Facilitating screening uptake is especially critical for Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer diagnoses and mortality while facing more obstacles to screening than non-Hispanic women. A clinically validated and accessible at-home SC alternative holds potential for meaningful impact and improved health outcomes within this community.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically high-risk HPV types, in the context of cervical cancer prevention among US Hispanic/Latinx women. The central question focuses on the acceptability, usability, and barriers to at-home self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for hrHPV testing compared to clinician-collected (CC) samples, and how these factors differ between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review reports a post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study, which enrolled women aged 25 to 65 years to perform self-collection of vaginal samples for hrHPV testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. A clinician-collected sample was obtained for method comparison. Participants completed usability and screening preference surveys. The study included 609 consented participants, with 603 using the SC device.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hispanic women reported significantly lower annual income, lower private insurance coverage, higher uninsured rates, and lower education levels compared to non-Hispanic women. Financial barriers were more pronounced for Hispanic women. Hispanic women expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC (78%) than non-Hispanic women (62%), and both groups reported a higher likelihood of staying up to date with screening using the at-home SC device, though non-Hispanic women to a lesser degree.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report significant differences in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening or delaying screening between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women, though English-not-primary-speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay screening (p = 0.22). The evidence does not report long-term clinical outcomes or diagnostic accuracy of the SC device compared to CC sampling.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need to address financial barriers and improve access to at-home SC devices to facilitate screening uptake among Hispanic women, who face disproportionate cervical cancer burden. Further research is needed to validate the clinical utility and diagnostic performance of the SC device in real-world settings and to evaluate its impact on reducing disparities in cervical cancer screening and outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the acceptability and usability of at-home self-collection (SC) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing among US Hispanic/Latinx women compared to clinician-collected (CC) samples. Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer, reported greater financial barriers and higher endorsement of SC (78%) than non-Hispanic women (62%). Both groups favored at-home SC for maintaining screening adherence, though non-Hispanic women were less enthusiastic. The study underscores the potential of SC to improve screening uptake in underserved populations but lacks evidence on long-term clinical outcomes or diagnostic accuracy.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述在美国西班牙裔/拉丁裔女性 宫颈癌 预防的背景下检查了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是 高危型HPV 类型。核心问题集中于与临床医生采集 (CC) 样本相比,在家自行采集 (SC) 阴道样本进行 hrHPV 检测的可接受性、可用性和障碍,以及这些因素在西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性之间有何不同。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述报告了 SELF-CERV 研究的事后分析,该研究招募了 25 至 65 岁的女性,在模拟家庭环境中使用独特的设备自行采集阴道样本进行 hrHPV 检测。获得临床医生收集的样本用于方法比较。参与者完成了可用性和筛选偏好调查。该研究包括 609 名同意的参与者,其中 603 人使用 SC 设备。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 与非西班牙裔女性相比,西班牙裔女性的年收入明显较低,私人保险覆盖范围较低,未参保率较高,教育水平较低。西班牙裔女性的经济障碍更为明显。西班牙裔女性对 SC 的认可度 (78%) 显着高于非西班牙裔女性 (62%),两组均表示使用家用 SC 设备及时了解最新情况的可能性更高,但非西班牙裔女性的程度较低。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述并未报告西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性在理解 宫颈癌 筛查或延迟筛查的目的方面存在显着差异,尽管非主要讲英语的西班牙裔女性更有可能推迟筛查 (p = 0.22)。证据并未报告 SC 设备与 CC 采样相比的长期临床结果或诊断准确性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要解决财务障碍并改善家庭 SC 设备的使用,以促进面临不成比例的 宫颈癌 负担的西班牙裔女性进行筛查。需要进一步的研究来验证 SC 设备在现实环境中的临床实用性和诊断性能,并评估其对减少 宫颈癌 筛查和结果差异的影响。

papers.title_zh: 美国西班牙裔/拉丁裔女性使用专为家庭收集而设计的设备进行 HPV 自我收集的经验。
papers.source_body_en: Background Cervical cancer is a preventable disease, and reaching populations who are under-screened and/or at highest risk is essential to the goal of disease elimination. Hispanic women in the US have a disproportionately higher incidence rate than non-Hispanic women. Objective Post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study of the unique experience and preferences among Hispanic compared to non-Hispanic participants with the goal of facilitating and improving screening and follow-up in more vulnerable populations. Methods Women 25 to 65 years who were enrolled performed self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. For method comparison, a clinician-collected (CC) sample was obtained. Participants also completed usability and screening preference surveys. Results A total of 609 participants were consented and 603 used the SC device. Of the 603 SC users, 115 (19.1%) identified themselves as Hispanic/Latinx. Compared to non-Hispanic women, Hispanic women, had significantly lower annual income (p < .001), a lower percentage of private insurance with more uninsured (p < .001) and lower levels of education (p < .001). There was no significant difference between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening. No difference was noted in delaying screening, although English Not Primary speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay (p = 0.22). Financial barriers were observed to be more of an impediment to Hispanic women compared to non-Hispanic women (p = 0.016). Negative experiences with in-clinic speculum exams were similar; however, Hispanic women (78%) expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC than non-Hispanic women (62%), (p = 0.001). Both populations reported that they would be more likely to stay up to date with cervical cancer screening with the at-home SC device, but non-Hispanic women to a significantly lesser degree (p = 0.002). In terms of assessing utility of telemedicine in screening, both populations reported similar engagement in healthcare activities, willingness to try new technology and current use of smartphones. Hispanic and non-Hispanic women were both nearly equally divided as to their preference for in-clinic visits vs telehealth. Conclusions Facilitating screening uptake is especially critical for Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer diagnoses and mortality while facing more obstacles to screening than non-Hispanic women. A clinically validated and accessible at-home SC alternative holds potential for meaningful impact and improved health outcomes within this community.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 宫颈癌 是一种可预防的疾病,覆盖筛查不足和/或风险最高的人群对于消除疾病的目标至关重要。美国的西班牙裔女性的 发病率 率比非西班牙裔女性高得不成比例。客观对 SELF-CERV 研究进行事后分析,了解西班牙裔参与者与非西班牙裔参与者相比的独特经历和偏好,目的是促进和改善对更弱势群体的筛查和随访。方法 入组的 25 至 65 岁女性在模拟家庭环境中使用独特的设备自行采集 (SC) 阴道样本,进行高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 检测。为了进行方法比较,获得了临床医生收集的 (CC) 样本。参与者还完成了可用性和筛选偏好调查。结果 共有 609 名参与者获得同意,其中 603 人使用了 SC 设备。在 603 名 SC 用户中,115 名 (19.1%) 认为自己是西班牙裔/拉丁裔。与非西班牙裔女性相比,西班牙裔女性的年收入显着较低 (p < .001),私人保险比例较低,未投保的人数较多 (p < .001),教育水平较低 (p < .001)。西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性对 宫颈癌 筛查目的的理解没有显着差异。尽管非主要讲英语的西班牙裔女性更有可能推迟筛查,但在推迟筛查方面没有发现差异(p = 0.22)。据观察,与非西班牙裔女性相比,经济障碍对西班牙裔女性的影响更大(p = 0.016)。诊所内窥镜检查的负面经历是相似的;然而,西班牙裔女性 (78%) 对 SC 的支持率明显高于非西班牙裔女性 (62%) (p = 0.001)。两个人群都报告称,她们更有可能通过家用 SC 设备了解最新的 宫颈癌 筛查,但非西班牙裔女性的程度明显较低 (p = 0.002)。在评估远程医疗在筛查中的效用方面,两个人群都报告了相似的医疗保健活动参与度、尝试新技术的意愿以及当前智能手​​机的使用情况。西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性对于门诊就诊与远程医疗的偏好几乎持平。结论 促进筛查对于西班牙裔女性尤其重要,她们承担着不成比例的 宫颈癌 诊断和 死亡率 负担,同时比非西班牙裔女性面临更多筛查障碍。经过临床验证且易于使用的家庭 SC 替代方案有可能对该社区产生有意义的影响并改善健康结果。

papers.title: HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Imaging Framework for AJCC Version 9 TNM Staging
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. Keywords: CT, MR Imaging, Head/Neck, Neck, Pharynx, Surgery, Human Papillomavirus, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Oropharynx, Transoral Robotic Surgery, Oropharyngeal Carcinoma, TTMV HPV DNA © RSNA, 2026.

papers.title: The State-of-the Art of Personalized Vaccines for Non-Communicable Diseases: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including cancer, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and allergic diseases, account for a significant amount of global morbidity and mortality. Chronic viral infections have not been recognized as NCDs, despite the availability of several therapeutic vaccination strategies against oncogenic viruses, such as the hepatitis B virus (HBV) and the human papillomavirus (HPV). Indeed, chronic viral infection leads to the development and progression of malignancies directly linked to the viruses. These considerations support a connection between NCDs, infectious diseases, and therapeutic vaccination. Recent advances in technology have paved the way to the use of vaccines beyond the prevention of infectious diseases, heralding innovative therapeutic and preventative strategies for a variety of chronic NCDs. Here we will review the state of the art of personalized vaccine strategies for NCDs, with an emphasis on the diverse technological platforms used to develop them, including mRNA and DNA vaccines, viral vectors, dendritic cell-based vaccines, nanoparticle delivery systems, and next-generation adjuvants. The review intends to make the case for personalized and antigen-specific vaccination strategies as a compelling option for precision immunotherapy primarily in oncology, where neoantigen-based vaccines are being developed. In addition, we will also review tolerogenic vaccination strategies, vaccination strategies targeting pathological proteins and pathways in neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, and vaccine-based treatment of chronic viral infections. Current evidence about vaccines suggests that several ways are available to induce an immune response or create tolerance to a disease, and possibly altering its course instead of simply controlling the symptoms. However, many challenges are still to be overcome, including disease variability, how to identify appropriate target antigens, the complexity of manufacturing process, long-term safety, and integration with already established treatments. By virtue of the convergence of multiple fields—immunology, genomics, bioinformatics, and new delivery systems—precision vaccinology is gaining momentum. Thus, it is envisaged that personalized vaccines will be an increasingly essential component of future preventive and therapeutic approaches for non-communicable diseases.

In addition, we will also review tolerogenic vaccination strategies, vaccination strategies targeting pathological proteins and pathways in neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, and vaccine-based treatment of chronic viral infections. Current evidence about vaccines suggests that several ways are available to induce an immune response or create tolerance to a disease, and possibly altering its course instead of simply controlling the symptoms. However, many challenges are still to be overcome, including disease variability, how to identify appropriate target antigens, the complexity of manufacturing process, long-term safety, and integration with already established treatments. By virtue of the convergence of multiple fields—immunology, genomics, bioinformatics, and new delivery systems—precision vaccinology is gaining momentum. Thus, it is envisaged that personalized vaccines will be an increasingly essential component of future preventive and therapeutic approaches for non-communicable diseases.

papers.title: Modelling the Effects of Smoking Behavior on Male-to-Male HPV Transmission and Anal Cancer Progression
papers.abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) has become a significant public health concern, particularly in countries where male vaccination is unavailable. Given the high susceptibility of MSM to HPV and anal cancer, and the unavailability of HPV vaccination for males in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), there is a need to identify alternative interventions for reducing disease transmission and burden in this population. The novel mathematical model presented in this article couples smoking behavior dynamics with HPV transmission and anal cancer progression among MSM. Smoking reduction is introduced as an intervention to assess its effects on disease transmission and burden. The basic reproduction number (R 0 ) is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and a global sensitivity analysis is performed using partial rank correlation coefficients (PRCC) to identify the influence of model parameters on RR 0 . Further, the theoretical analysis of the model reveals a backward bifurcation, implying that RR 0 < 1 is necessary but not sufficient to eradicate the disease. The study finds that smoking reduction among MSM reduces HPV infection and anal cancer burden relative to baseline projections without intervention. The joint effect of smoking reduction and vaccination shows that the critical vaccination coverage needed to achieve RR 0 <1 decreases as the level of smoking reduction increases. A similar outcome is observed for contact reduction. These findings highlight the importance of concurrent interventions, which can significantly curtail the spread of HPV and reduce disease burden in both the high-risk group and the general population.

papers.abstract_original: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) has become a significant public health concern, particularly in countries where male vaccination is unavailable. Given the high susceptibility of MSM to HPV and anal cancer, and the unavailability of HPV vaccination for males in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), there is a need to identify alternative interventions for reducing disease transmission and burden in this population. The novel mathematical model presented in this article couples smoking behavior dynamics with HPV transmission and anal cancer progression among MSM. Smoking reduction is introduced as an intervention to assess its effects on disease transmission and burden. The basic reproduction number (R 0 ) is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and a global sensitivity analysis is performed using partial rank correlation coefficients (PRCC) to identify the influence of model parameters on RR 0 . Further, the theoretical analysis of the model reveals a backward bifurcation, implying that RR 0 < 1 is necessary but not sufficient to eradicate the disease. The study finds that smoking reduction among MSM reduces HPV infection and anal cancer burden relative to baseline projections without intervention. The joint effect of smoking reduction and vaccination shows that the critical vaccination coverage needed to achieve RR 0 <1 decreases as the level of smoking reduction increases. A similar outcome is observed for contact reduction. These findings highlight the importance of concurrent interventions, which can significantly curtail the spread of HPV and reduce disease burden in both the high-risk group and the general population.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of smoking behavior on HPV transmission and anal cancer progression among men who have sex with men (MSM). It presents a novel mathematical model that integrates smoking dynamics with HPV spread and disease outcomes. The research highlights the potential of smoking reduction as an intervention to lower HPV infection and anal cancer burden in this population. The model's analysis reveals a backward bifurcation, indicating that reducing the basic reproduction number below one is not enough to eliminate the disease. The study also demonstrates that combining smoking reduction with vaccination can significantly lower the required vaccination coverage for disease control. These findings emphasize the importance of addressing smoking behavior alongside vaccination to mitigate HPV-related health risks in MSM communities.

papers.abstract_zh: 男男性行为者 (MSM) 中的 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染已成为一个重大的公共卫生问题,特别是在无法获得男性 疫苗接种 的国家。鉴于 MSM 对 HPV 和肛门癌的高度易感性,以及低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 男性无法获得 HPV 传播,因此需要确定替代干预措施来减少该人群的疾病 传播 和负担。本文提出的新颖数学模型将吸烟行为动态与 HPV 传播 和 MSM 中肛门癌的进展联系起来。减少吸烟作为一项干预措施被引入,以评估其对疾病 传播 和负担的影响。采用下一代矩阵法推导基本再生数(R 0 ),并利用偏秩相关系数(PRCC)进行全局敏感性分析,以确定模型参数对RR 0 的影响。此外,模型的理论分析揭示了后向分歧,这意味着 RR 0 < 1 对于根除疾病是必要的,但不足以消除。研究发现,相对于没有干预的基线预测,MSM 中吸烟的减少可以减少 HPV 感染和肛门癌负担。减少吸烟和疫苗接种的联合效应表明,随着吸烟减少水平的增加,实现RR 0 <1所需的临界疫苗接种覆盖率降低。减少接触也观察到类似的结果。这些发现强调了同时干预措施的重要性,这可以显着减少 HPV 的传播并减轻高危人群和普通人群的疾病负担。

papers.title: First-in-Human, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Phase 1 Study to Assess in Healthy Adults the Safety and Immunogenicity of Intramuscularly Administered AAVLP-HPV Vaccine
papers.abstract: Abstract Seeking a simple vaccine to protect against all cancer-associated human papillomaviruses (HPV), L2 residues 17-36 of both HPV16 and HPV31 displayed on the surface of an Adeno-Associated Virus-Like Particle (AAVLP-HPV) was developed. Here, a phase 1 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical study has been conducted in 20 male and female subjects at a single dose level (20μg) without an adjuvant. AAVLP-HPV vaccine administration was safe and well tolerated. Repeat vaccination with AAVLP-HPV elicited L2-specific neutralizing antibodies of modest titer in serum. Antibodies cross-reactive with L2 of diverse HPV types were detected, but responses were weak in most vaccinees. We conclude that while AAVLP-HPV vaccination is well tolerated, an adjuvant is likely needed to consistently elicit durable and broadly neutralizing responses. One sentence summary Vaccination with AAVLP-HPV is safe and immunogenic in healthy adults. Funding The study was funded by 2A Pharma AB. MM and RBSR were funded by service contracts from 2A Pharma AB. RBSR and JA were funded by Public Health Service (grants.nih.gov) grant P50 CA098252.

papers.title: Clinical Impact of HPV Self-Sampling and Molecular Biomarkers on Cervical Cancer Screening and Triage: “The Times They Are A-Changin’”—A Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a necessary but insufficient cause of cervical cancer (CC) and reflects a long-standing host–virus equilibrium shaped by immune control, viral persistence, and latency. The transition from cytology-based screening to primary high-risk HPV testing has substantially improved early detection of cervical precancerous lesions but has also introduced new clinical challenges related to fluctuating test results, overdiagnosis, overtreatment, and patient anxiety, whose magnitude may vary across countries depending on screening organization and access to prevention services. This narrative review provides a clinically oriented overview of HPV-based CC screening in the context of evolving knowledge on HPV natural history, persistence, and immune interaction, and discusses the implications for the interpretation of test results and risk stratification. New emerging screening and triage approaches, including molecular biomarkers, exosome-based biomarkers, and artificial-intelligence-supported risk assessment, are reshaping CC prevention strategies by enabling more precise identification of women at risk for clinically significant disease. These tools may be particularly relevant in self-sampling-based screening pathways, where molecular triage strategies can reduce the need for additional clinician-collected samples and improve management of HPV-positive women. At the same time, improved understanding of viral latency and host-related determinants of progression supports a shift from binary test interpretation toward longitudinal and individualized risk assessment. Integrating biological insight with technological innovation may facilitate personalized screening strategies that maintain high sensitivity while reducing unnecessary interventions. An evolutionary-informed and risk-adapted approach to HPV-related disease management is essential to optimize prevention outcomes and preserve the benefits of population-based screening programs.

source_records.title: Clinical Impact of HPV Self-Sampling and Molecular Biomarkers on Cervical Cancer Screening and Triage: “The Times They Are A-Changin’”—A Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives
source_records.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a necessary but insufficient cause of cervical cancer (CC) and reflects a long-standing host–virus equilibrium shaped by immune control, viral persistence, and latency. The transition from cytology-based screening to primary high-risk HPV testing has substantially improved early detection of cervical precancerous lesions but has also introduced new clinical challenges related to fluctuating test results, overdiagnosis, overtreatment, and patient anxiety, whose magnitude may vary across countries depending on screening organization and access to prevention services. This narrative review provides a clinically oriented overview of HPV-based CC screening in the context of evolving knowledge on HPV natural history, persistence, and immune interaction, and discusses the implications for the interpretation of test results and risk stratification. New emerging screening and triage approaches, including molecular biomarkers, exosome-based biomarkers, and artificial-intelligence-supported risk assessment, are reshaping CC prevention strategies by enabling more precise identification of women at risk for clinically significant disease. These tools may be particularly relevant in self-sampling-based screening pathways, where molecular triage strategies can reduce the need for additional clinician-collected samples and improve management of HPV-positive women. At the same time, improved understanding of viral latency and host-related determinants of progression supports a shift from binary test interpretation toward longitudinal and individualized risk assessment. Integrating biological insight with technological innovation may facilitate personalized screening strategies that maintain high sensitivity while reducing unnecessary interventions. An evolutionary-informed and risk-adapted approach to HPV-related disease management is essential to optimize prevention outcomes and preserve the benefits of population-based screening programs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 HPV 自我采样和分子生物标志物对 宫颈癌 筛查和分诊的临床影响,重点关注 HPV 感染的自然史、其持续性、免疫相互作用以及对风险分层和癌前病变早期检测的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对现有文献的叙述性综合,没有明确提及系统搜索方法、数据库或荟萃分析。它讨论了从基于细胞学的筛查到初级 HPV 检测的转变、这种转变带来的挑战以及新筛查和分诊方法的潜力。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,转向基于 HPV 的筛查改善了宫颈癌前病变的早期检测,但也带来了检测结果波动、过度诊断和过度治疗等挑战。由于 HPV 感染的复杂性及其与 宿主 免疫系统的相互作用,它强调需要进行纵向和个体化的风险评估。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于 HPV 检测结果的解释存在争议,特别是在结果波动和过度诊断风险的背景下。该综述强调需要更好地了解影响疾病进展的病毒潜伏期和 宿主 相关因素,以及整合分子生物标志物和人工智能以进行更精确的风险评估。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论表明,将生物学见解与分子生物标志物和人工智能等技术创新相结合,可以改善个性化筛查策略。它还强调了制定风险适应方法来管理 HPV 相关疾病的重要性,以优化预防结果并保持基于人群的筛查计划的有效性。

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 (CC) 的必要但不充分的原因,反映了由免疫控制、病毒持久性和潜伏期形成的长期 宿主 病毒平衡。从基于细胞学的筛查到初级 高危型HPV 检测的转变极大地改善了宫颈癌前病变的早期发现,但也带来了与检测结果波动、过度诊断、过度治疗和患者焦虑相关的新的临床挑战,其程度可能因国家而异,具体取决于筛查组织和预防服务的获取情况。这篇叙述性综述在 HPV 自然史、持久性和免疫相互作用的知识不断发展的背景下,对基于 HPV 的 CC 筛查进行了临床导向的概述,并讨论了对检测结果和风险分层解释的影响。新出现的筛查和分诊方法,包括分子生物标志物、基于外泌体的生物标志物和人工智能支持的风险评估,正在重塑 CC 预防策略,能够更准确地识别面临临床重大疾病风险的女性。这些工具可能与基于自我采样的筛查途径特别相关,其中分子分类策略可以减少对临床医生收集额外样本的需求,并改善对 HPV 阳性女性的管理。与此同时,对病毒潜伏期和 宿主 相关进展决定因素的更好理解支持从二元测试解释向纵向和个体化风险评估的转变。将生物学洞察力与技术创新相结合可能有助于个性化筛查策略,保持高灵敏度,同时减少不必要的干预。HPV 相关疾病管理的进化信息和风险适应方法对于优化预防结果和保持基于人群的筛查计划的益处至关重要。

papers.title: Deciphering the Molecular Landscape of Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Anal Canal: From Biology to Precision Oncology
papers.abstract: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC) is a rare malignancy whose incidence has been steadily increasing worldwide. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, is the main etiological factor and plays a central role in tumor development. While combined chemoradiotherapy remains the standard treatment for localized disease and achieves high rates of tumor control, a considerable proportion of patients experience recurrence or present with advanced disease. For the latter, therapeutic options remain limited. Over the last decade, advances in genomic profiling have significantly expanded our understanding of SCAC biology. Recurrent alterations affecting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, especially PIK3CA mutations, have emerged as the most common molecular events, particularly in HPV-positive tumors. Additional alterations involve receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, chromatin remodeling genes, DNA damage response pathways, and components of the MAPK cascade. Moreover, HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors display distinct molecular features with important prognostic implications. Immunotherapy has recently become an important component of treatment for advanced SCAC, although reliable predictive biomarkers are still lacking. This review summarizes the current evidence on the molecular landscape of SCAC, discusses emerging prognostic and predictive biomarkers, and highlights potential opportunities for the development of more personalized therapeutic strategies.

It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that persistent infection with high-risk HPV, especially HPV16 and HPV18, is the main etiological factor in SCAC. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while combined chemoradiotherapy is the standard treatment for localized SCAC, a considerable proportion of patients experience recurrence or present with advanced disease. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注肛管鳞状细胞癌 (SCAC) 的分子概况,重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的作用,特别是 高危型HPV 类型,例如 HPV16 和 HPV18。核心问题是了解 SCAC 发生和进展的分子机制,并探索这些发现对精准肿瘤学的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 SCAC 分子特征现有文献的叙述性综合,重点关注 HPV 相关机制。它不报告特定的数据库、搜索日期或荟萃分析方法。证据来自该领域的一般观察和发现,没有明确提及研究选择标准或定量分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述认为,高危型HPV,尤其是HPV16和HPV18的持续感染是SCAC的主要病因。它强调,PI3K/AKT/mTOR 通路的反复改变,特别是 PIK3CA 突变,是 HPV 阳性肿瘤中最常见的分子事件。此外,HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性肿瘤表现出不同的分子特征,具有重要的预后意义。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,虽然联合放化疗是局部 SCAC 的标准 治疗,但相当一部分患者会出现复发或出现晚期疾病。它还提到晚期疾病的治疗选择仍然有限。此外,该综述还发现,晚期 SCAC 免疫治疗缺乏可靠的预测生物标志物。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步研究 SCAC 的分子机制,特别是在 HPV 阳性肿瘤中,以开发更个性化的治疗策略。它还强调了识别免疫治疗的可靠预测生物标志物以及改进 监测 和 HPV 相关癌症的诊断方法的重要性。

papers.abstract_zh: 肛管鳞状细胞癌(SCAC)是一种罕见的恶性肿瘤,其发病率在全球范围内一直在稳步增长。高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV),特别是HPV16和HPV18基因型的持续感染,是主要的病因,在肿瘤的发生发展中发挥着核心作用。虽然联合放化疗仍然是局部疾病的标准 治疗 并实现了较高的肿瘤控制率,但相当一部分患者出现复发或出现晚期疾病。对于后者,治疗选择仍然有限。在过去的十年中,基因组分析的进步极大地扩展了我们对 SCAC 生物学的理解。影响 PI3K/AKT/mTOR 通路的反复改变,尤其是 PIK3CA 突变,已成为最常见的分子事件,特别是在 HPV 阳性肿瘤中。其他改变涉及受体酪氨酸激酶信号传导、染色质重塑基因、DNA 损伤反应途径和 MAPK 级联的组成部分。此外,HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性肿瘤表现出不同的分子特征,具有重要的预后意义。尽管仍然缺乏可靠的预测生物标志物,但免疫疗法最近已成为 治疗 治疗晚期 SCAC 的重要组成部分。这篇综述总结了 SCAC 分子格局的当前证据,讨论了新兴的预后和预测生物标志物,并强调了开发更个性化治疗策略的潜在机会。

papers.title: Research progress on the association between vaginal Lactobacillus iners and cervical cancer
papers.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk Human Papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the central etiological factor in cervical cancer, while the host vaginal microenvironment plays a critical role in disease progression. Lactobacillus iners is one of the most widely distributed lactobacilli in the vagina. Because of its unique biological features, including exclusive production of L-lactic acid and a small genome, it occupies a transitional state within the vaginal ecosystem. Recent studies have shown that Lactobacillus iners (L. iners) plays dual and paradoxical roles in cervical carcinogenesis and progression. In the vaginal microenvironment, L. iners is associated with persistent hrHPV infection and an increased risk of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) progression; its protective effects are limited and often coexist with unfavorable inflammatory states. In contrast, within the tumor microenvironment, intratumoral colonization by L. iners can markedly increase L-lactate production, induce chemoradiotherapy resistance in tumor cells, and serve as an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. This review systematically summarizes the biological characteristics of L. iners, its roles and mechanisms in cervical cancer initiation, progression, and treatment resistance, and its translational value as a novel biomarker and potential therapeutic target. Current controversies, limitations, and future directions are also discussed.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical technology and theory.

source_records.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk Human Papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the central etiological factor in cervical cancer, while the host vaginal microenvironment plays a critical role in disease progression. Lactobacillus iners is one of the most widely distributed lactobacilli in the vagina. Because of its unique biological features, including exclusive production of L-lactic acid and a small genome, it occupies a transitional state within the vaginal ecosystem. Recent studies have shown that Lactobacillus iners (L. iners) plays dual and paradoxical roles in cervical carcinogenesis and progression. In the vaginal microenvironment, L. iners is associated with persistent hrHPV infection and an increased risk of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) progression; its protective effects are limited and often coexist with unfavorable inflammatory states. In contrast, within the tumor microenvironment, intratumoral colonization by L. iners can markedly increase L-lactate production, induce chemoradiotherapy resistance in tumor cells, and serve as an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. This review systematically summarizes the biological characteristics of L. iners, its roles and mechanisms in cervical cancer initiation, progression, and treatment resistance, and its translational value as a novel biomarker and potential therapeutic target. Current controversies, limitations, and future directions are also discussed.

papers.title: Community-Identified Barriers and Strategies for Improving HPV Vaccination in South Texas
papers.abstract: Bexar County is a South Texas county with low human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates, which hinders efforts to prevent HPV-related cancers. We conducted a community assessment from the perspective of community members who administer social/health services and/or coalitions in Bexar County. We aimed to assess perceived barriers and possible community solutions to HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Data were collected using an online quantitative survey measuring knowledge and attitudes toward HPV vaccination based on the Increasing Vaccination Model, as well as perceived barriers to HPV vaccination and potential solutions to improve vaccination. Participants included persons administering social/health services/part of coalitions in Bexar County from January to March 2025 ( N = 45). Descriptive statistics were estimated. Most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated for HPV. Primary barriers at the organizational level were competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. Participants were asked to consider what community-level strategies could be deployed to increase HPV vaccination; the highest rated were mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine. There is a strong community interest in improving HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Developing a multi-component intervention that addresses direct access issues, coupled with provider recommendations, could surmount the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in this community.

The central question is about understanding community-level challenges and potential solutions to enhance HPV vaccination.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a community assessment using an online quantitative survey targeting individuals who administer social/health services or are part of coalitions in Bexar County. Data were collected from January to March 2025, involving 45 participants. Descriptive statistics were estimated to analyze the findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated. The main conclusion is that a multi-component intervention addressing direct access issues and provider recommendations could overcome the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in the community.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identified primary barriers at the organizational level, including competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for community-level strategies such as mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine to improve HPV vaccination rates. analysis.summary_en: This review explores barriers and strategies for improving HPV vaccination rates in Bexar County, South Texas. It identifies organizational-level challenges such as competing health priorities, provider knowledge gaps, language barriers, and patient awareness issues. The study emphasizes the importance of community engagement and multi-component interventions to address these barriers. Key strategies include mobile vaccination units, public awareness campaigns, and financial support for the vaccine. The findings suggest a strong community interest in increasing HPV vaccination rates, particularly among 9- to 26-year-olds, and highlight the need for targeted research and practice improvements to achieve this goal.

elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a community assessment using an online quantitative survey targeting individuals who administer social/health services or are part of coalitions in Bexar County. Data were collected from January to March 2025, involving 45 participants. Descriptive statistics were estimated to analyze the findings.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated. The main conclusion is that a multi-component intervention addressing direct access issues and provider recommendations could overcome the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in the community.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identified primary barriers at the organizational level, including competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. However, the evidence does not report on specific controversies or unresolved mechanisms related to HPV.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for community-level strategies such as mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine to improve HPV vaccination rates. It also suggests the importance of addressing access issues and provider training to enhance vaccination efforts.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),旨在找出改善南德克萨斯州贝克萨尔县 HPV 疫苗接种 率的障碍和策略,特别是在 9 至 26 岁的人群中。核心问题是了解社区层面的挑战和增强 HPV 疫苗接种 的潜在解决方案。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查使用在线定量调查对贝克萨尔县管理社会/卫生服务或联盟成员的个人进行了社区评估。数据收集时间为 2025 年 1 月至 3 月,涉及 45 名参与者。估计描述性统计数据以分析结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查发现,大多数参与者强烈同意 HPV 疫苗接种 率可以提高,并且对于 9 至 26 岁的人来说接种疫苗非常重要。主要结论是,解决直接获取问题和提供者建议的多成分干预措施可以克服​​社区中 HPV 疫苗接种 所报告的障碍。

papers.title_zh: 德克萨斯州南部社区确定的改善 HPV 疫苗接种 的障碍和策略
papers.source_body_en: Bexar County is a South Texas county with low human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates, which hinders efforts to prevent HPV-related cancers. We conducted a community assessment from the perspective of community members who administer social/health services and/or coalitions in Bexar County. We aimed to assess perceived barriers and possible community solutions to HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Data were collected using an online quantitative survey measuring knowledge and attitudes toward HPV vaccination based on the Increasing Vaccination Model, as well as perceived barriers to HPV vaccination and potential solutions to improve vaccination. Participants included persons administering social/health services/part of coalitions in Bexar County from January to March 2025 ( N = 45). Descriptive statistics were estimated. Most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated for HPV. Primary barriers at the organizational level were competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. Participants were asked to consider what community-level strategies could be deployed to increase HPV vaccination; the highest rated were mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine. There is a strong community interest in improving HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Developing a multi-component intervention that addresses direct access issues, coupled with provider recommendations, could surmount the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in this community.

papers.title: Integrating HPV self-sampling into antenatal care: prevalence, genotype distribution, clinical outcomes, and preventive implications among pregnant women in Thailand
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, particularly in low- and middle-income countries with limited screening coverage. Pregnancy offers an opportunity to integrate preventive interventions into antenatal care (ANC). Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling may improve participation by reducing barriers to conventional screening. OBJECTIVE This study evaluated HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, clinical outcomes, and the feasibility of HPV self-sampling in ANC among pregnant women in Thailand. STUDY DESIGN: This prospective observational study enrolled pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years with a gestational age ≥ 12 weeks attending ANC at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. Data were collected from July 21, 2025, to January 10, 2026. After standardized instruction, participants performed vaginal HPV self-sampling. HPV was detected and genotyped using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction. Outcomes included HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, acceptance, and follow-up among HPV-positive participants. RESULTS Of 644 pregnant women, HPV infection was detected in 147 (overall prevalence, 22.8%). Among HPV-positive participants, HPV16/18 infection was identified in 37 cases (25.2%) and non-16/18 infection in 110 cases (74.8%). HPV52 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by HPV16, HPV66, HPV51, and HPV68. Younger maternal age, lower income, divorced/separated/widowed status, and smoking-related exposure were independently associated with HPV infection. Notably, 62.4% of participants had never undergone cervical cancer screening. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, mainly for its convenience and ease of use. CONCLUSION HPV self-sampling integrated into ANC was feasible and acceptable among pregnant women. ANC may extend cervical cancer screening to previously underscreened women and support prevention strategies.

STUDY DESIGN: This prospective observational study enrolled pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years with a gestational age ≥ 12 weeks attending ANC at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. CONCLUSION HPV self-sampling integrated into ANC was feasible and acceptable among pregnant women. papers.title: Acceptability of At-Home hrHPV Cervical Cancer Screening For Transmasculine Individuals: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transmasculine individuals are less likely to complete cervical cancer screening than cisgender individuals, thus increasing their risk for cervical cancer. Multidimensional socioecological determinants may contribute to cervical cancer disparities for transgender people. OBJECTIVE: This study explored cervical cancer screening barriers and facilitators, acceptability of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening, and cervical cancer health promotion methods among transmasculine individuals. METHODS: This qualitative description examined socioecological factors affecting cervical cancer screening in transmasculine individuals in 2022 to 2023. Through purposive sampling, 9 participants were interviewed in-depth using semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: Cervical cancer screening decisions were shaped by socioecological barriers and facilitators, including dysphoria, negative healthcare experiences, and exclusionary clinical spaces, alongside healthcare provider support and social network encouragement. At-home hrHPV self-sampling was conditionally acceptable and valued for autonomy and privacy. Affirming communication and culturally competent healthcare providers were central to effective cervical cancer screening promotion. CONCLUSION: Addressing these findings requires an approach that integrates healthcare provider and staff LGBTQ+-specific training, cultural humility, patient-centered care, affirming healthcare provider communication, targeted LGBTQ+-specific education, hrHPV self-sampling options, inclusive clinical environments, cervical cancer screening cost and coverage solutions, and healthcare systems that identify cervical cancer screening eligibility by anatomy. By addressing multilevel socioecological barriers while amplifying patient-identified facilitators such as autonomy, privacy, trusted provider recommendations, and social support; healthcare providers and systems can improve equitable access to cervical cancer screening and reduce preventable cervical cancer disparities among transmasculine and other underscreened populations.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:与顺性别个体相比,跨男性个体完成 宫颈癌 筛查的可能性较小,因此增加了他们患 宫颈癌 的风险。多维社会生态决定因素可能会导致跨性别者的 宫颈癌 差异。目的:本研究探讨了 宫颈癌 筛查的障碍和促进因素、高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 在家自我采样 宫颈癌 筛查的可接受性,以及跨男性个体中的 宫颈癌 健康促进方法。方法:本定性描述研究了 2022 年至 2023 年影响跨男性个体 宫颈癌 筛查的社会生态因素。通过有目的抽样,使用半结构化访谈对 9 名参与者进行了深入访谈。使用主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:宫颈癌 筛查决策是由社会生态障碍和促进因素决定的,包括烦躁不安、负面医疗体验和排斥性临床空间,以及医疗保健提供者的支持和社交网络鼓励。家庭 hrHPV 自我采样是有条件接受的,并且重视自主性和隐私性。肯定沟通和具有文化能力的医疗保健提供者是有效 宫颈癌 筛查推广的核心。结论:解决这些发现需要一种方法,将医疗保健提供者和员工 LGBTQ+ 特定培训、文化谦逊、以患者为中心的护理、确认医疗保健提供者沟通、有针对性的 LGBTQ+ 特定教育、hrHPV 自我采样选项、包容性临床环境、宫颈癌 筛查成本和覆盖解决方案以及通过解剖学识别 宫颈癌 筛查资格的医疗保健系统相结合。通过解决多层次的社会生态障碍,同时扩大患者识别的促进因素,例如自主性、隐私、值得信赖的提供者建议和社会支持;医疗保健提供者和系统可以改善 宫颈癌 筛查的公平性,并减少跨男性和其他筛查不足人群之间可预防的 宫颈癌 差异。

papers.title: Liquid Biopsy for Minimal Residual Disease Assessment in Endometrial and Cervical Cancers: Molecular Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Translational Barriers
papers.abstract: Endometrial and cervical cancers can recur from subclinical disease not evident on routine surveillance. This narrative review critically evaluates liquid biopsy for minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment and recurrence monitoring. Post-treatment human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in cervical cancer has the strongest disease-specific prospective evidence of clinical validity; persistent detection is strongly associated with recurrence, but moderate sensitivity and false-negative results do not support treatment de-escalation on negativity alone. With regard to endometrial cancer, perioperative ctDNA has prognostic support from an 11-study, 1298-patient meta-analysis and additional cohorts, although assay heterogeneity and limited independent replication constrain clinical readiness. Postoperative positivity generally shows stronger associations than preoperative detection. Cervicovaginal and urine DNA-methylation studies provide preliminary evidence for detecting established recurrence, especially local recurrence, but not prospective molecular lead time or clinical utility. Digital PCR, disease-specific fixed panels, tumor-informed assays, and error-corrected sequencing serve distinct settings; broad pan-cancer plasma profiling remains mainly an advanced-disease tool. Circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics remain exploratory. Liquid biopsy should remain an investigational adjunct until prospective trials show that acting on molecular findings improves outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review evaluates liquid biopsy biomarkers, particularly HPV-specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), for minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment and recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated cancers, including cervical and endometrial cancers. The strongest evidence supports the clinical validity of post-treatment HPV ctDNA in cervical cancer, where persistent detection correlates with recurrence, though moderate sensitivity and false negatives limit its use for treatment de-escalation. In endometrial cancer, perioperative ctDNA shows prognostic value, supported by a meta-analysis of 1,298 patients, but assay heterogeneity and limited replication hinder clinical adoption. Postoperative ctDNA positivity is more strongly associated with outcomes than preoperative detection. Preliminary evidence exists for cervicovaginal and urine DNA-methylation assays in detecting recurrence, but prospective utility remains unproven. Circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics are exploratory. The review concludes that liquid biopsy should remain investigational until prospective trials demonstrate improved outcomes from acting on molecular findings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述在液体活检的背景下检查了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是高危类型(例如 HPV16、HPV18、HPV31、HPV33、HPV45、HPV52、HPV58)及其相关疾病(例如宫颈上皮内瘤变、HPV 相关 宫颈癌、尖锐湿疣),以进行微小残留病 (MRD) 评估和复发监控。核心问题集中在 HPV 特异性 ctDNA 和其他液体活检生物标志物在 治疗 监测 后和预后中的临床有效性和实用性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,评估用于 HPV 相关癌症 MRD 评估的液体活检方法。它综合了 ctDNA、循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤教育血小板和片段组学的证据,强调了它们在宫颈癌和子宫内膜癌中的作用。该综述没有明确报告系统检索日期、数据库或资格标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 治疗 后的 宫颈癌 中的 HPV 循环肿瘤 DNA (ctDNA) 显示出最强的疾病特异性临床有效性前瞻性证据;持续检测与复发密切相关。然而,中等敏感性和假阴性结果排除了仅基于阴性结果的 治疗 降级。在子宫内膜癌中,围手术期 ctDNA 得到了 11 项研究、1298 名患者的荟萃分析和额外的 队列研究 的预后支持,尽管检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。术后 ctDNA 阳性通常表现出比术前检测更强的与结果的关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 子宫内膜癌中 ctDNA 的检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。对于 宫颈癌,ctDNA 检测的中等灵敏度和假阴性结果限制了其在 治疗 降级中的效用。宫颈阴道和尿液 DNA 甲基化研究为检测复发提供了初步证据,但缺乏前瞻性的分子前置时间或临床实用性。循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤培养血小板和片段组学仍处于探索阶段,尚未确定临床有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 液体活检应继续作为研究的辅助手段,直到前瞻性试验证明根据分子发现采取行动可以改善患者的预后。未来的研究应优先考虑标准化、疾病特异性检测,并具有经过验证的临床决策阈值,特别是针对 HPV 相关的宫颈癌和子宫内膜癌。需要进行前瞻性研究来确定 ctDNA 和其他生物标志物在指导 治疗 调整和 监测 策略方面的临床效用。

papers.abstract_zh: 子宫内膜和 宫颈癌 可能会因常规 监测 上不明显的亚临床疾病而复发。这篇叙述性综述批判性地评价了液体活检用于微小残留病(MRD)评估和复发监测的作用。治疗 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)后的宫颈癌中的循环肿瘤DNA(ctDNA)具有最强的疾病特异性临床有效性前瞻性证据;持续检测与复发密切相关,但中等敏感性和假阴性结果并不支持 治疗 仅根据阴性情况进行降级。对于子宫内膜癌,围手术期 ctDNA 得到了 11 项研究、1298 名患者的荟萃分析和额外的 队列研究 的预后支持,尽管检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。术后阳性通常表现出比术前检测更强的关联性。宫颈阴道和尿液 DNA 甲基化研究为检测已确定的复发(尤其是局部复发)提供了初步证据,但没有提供预期的分子前置时间或临床效用。数字 PCR、疾病特异性固定试剂盒、肿瘤信息检测和纠错测序服务于不同的环境;广泛的全癌血浆分析仍然主要是一种晚期疾病工具。循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤培养的血小板和片段组学仍处于探索阶段。液体活检应继续作为研究的辅助手段,直到前瞻性试验表明根据分子发现采取行动可以改善结果。

papers.title: Cell-resolved virus-host programs across cancers associated with five human oncoviruses: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing can separate transcriptional changes within a cell type from shifts in tumor composition, yet findings from virus-associated cancers remain scattered across diseases and study designs. Human single-cell RNA-sequencing studies were reviewed, including cancers associated with human papillomavirus (HPV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), or Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV). PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for reports published from 2020 to 2 August 2026, with complementary coverage checks in Scopus and Web of Science. Seventy-five reports met the eligibility criteria (HPV, 34; EBV, 14; HBV, 18; HTLV-1, 5; MCPyV, 4). Findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature. Instead, several functions recurred in different cellular compartments: interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and B-cell or tertiary-lymphoid organization were accompanied by checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, regulatory T cells, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and loss of antigen presentation. Within malignant cells, viral transcript abundance was associated with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response, although these relationships varied by virus, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy. More informative studies combined cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, etiologically matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation. These design features will be necessary if cell-resolved virus-host programs are to yield reproducible biomarkers.

source_records.title: Cell-resolved virus-host programs across cancers associated with five human oncoviruses: a systematic review
source_records.abstract: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing can separate transcriptional changes within a cell type from shifts in tumor composition, yet findings from virus-associated cancers remain scattered across diseases and study designs. Human single-cell RNA-sequencing studies were reviewed, including cancers associated with human papillomavirus (HPV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), or Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV). PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for reports published from 2020 to 2 August 2026, with complementary coverage checks in Scopus and Web of Science. Seventy-five reports met the eligibility criteria (HPV, 34; EBV, 14; HBV, 18; HTLV-1, 5; MCPyV, 4). Findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature. Instead, several functions recurred in different cellular compartments: interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and B-cell or tertiary-lymphoid organization were accompanied by checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, regulatory T cells, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and loss of antigen presentation. Within malignant cells, viral transcript abundance was associated with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response, although these relationships varied by virus, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy. More informative studies combined cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, etiologically matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation. These design features will be necessary if cell-resolved virus-host programs are to yield reproducible biomarkers.

papers.title_original: Cell-resolved virus-host programs across cancers associated with five human oncoviruses: a systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing to resolve virus-host transcriptional programs, focusing on HPV types (e.g., HPV16, HPV18) and HPV-associated diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. The central question addresses how cell-resolved transcriptional changes in HPV-positive tumors differ from shifts in tumor composition and what recurrent host-gene functions emerge across these cancers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic synthesis of human single-cell RNA-sequencing studies published from 2020 to 2 August 2026, identified via PubMed/MEDLINE with complementary checks in Scopus and Web of Science. Eligibility criteria included studies on HPV, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), or Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV), with 75 reports meeting inclusion criteria (HPV: 34 reports).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across HPV-associated cancers, recurrent host-gene functions include interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and B-cell or tertiary-lymphoid organization, alongside checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, regulatory T cells, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and loss of antigen presentation. Within malignant HPV-positive cells, viral transcript abundance correlates variably with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response depending on virus type, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature across HPV-associated cancers, indicating heterogeneity in transcriptional programs. The review highlights that studies lacking cell-level viral-read assignment, patient-level analysis with etiologically matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation are less informative and may contribute to inconsistent conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: To yield reproducible biomarkers from cell-resolved virus-host programs in HPV-associated cancers, future studies should integrate cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, include etiologically matched controls, employ spatial or longitudinal sampling, and incorporate orthogonal validation. Design features such as these are necessary to overcome current heterogeneity and improve biomarker reliability.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes single-cell RNA-sequencing studies of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers published from 2020 to 2026, focusing on HPV types (e.g., HPV16, HPV18) and diseases including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. Across 34 HPV-focused studies, recurrent host-gene functions included interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and tertiary-lymphoid organization, alongside immune checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, and suppressive myeloid states. Within malignant HPV-positive cells, viral transcript abundance correlated variably with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response depending on virus type, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy. The review emphasizes that findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature, reflecting heterogeneity in transcriptional programs. It concludes that reproducible biomarkers will require studies combining cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述使用单细胞 RNA 测序来解析病毒 宿主 转录程序,检查 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关癌症,重点关注 HPV 类型(例如 HPV16、HPV18)和 HPV 相关疾病,如宫颈上皮内瘤变和 HPV 相关宫颈癌、肛门癌和口咽癌。核心问题涉及 HPV 阳性肿瘤中细胞解析的转录变化与肿瘤组成的变化有何不同,以及这些癌症中出现的复发性 宿主 基因功能。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 2020 年至 2026 年 8 月 2 日发表的人类单细胞 RNA 测序研究的系统综合,通过 PubMed/MEDLINE 进行鉴定,并在 Scopus 和 Web of Science 中进行补充检查。资格标准包括针对 HPV、EB 病毒 (EBV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、人类 T 细胞白血病病毒 1 型 (HTLV-1) 或默克尔细胞多瘤病毒 (MCPyV) 的研究,其中 75 份报告符合纳入标准(HPV:34 份报告)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在 HPV 相关癌症中,复发性 宿主 基因功能包括干扰素反应、抗原呈递、克隆淋巴细胞扩增和 B 细胞或三级淋巴组织,以及检查点、T 细胞耗竭、调节性 T 细胞、抑制性骨髓和基质状态以及抗原呈递丧失。在恶性 HPV 阳性细胞内,病毒转录本丰度与分化、整合、增殖、侵袭或 治疗 反应存在不同的相关性,具体取决于病毒类型、谱系、组织、疾病阶段和治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究结果并未集中在 HPV 相关癌症的单一 宿主 基因特征上,这表明转录程序存在异质性。该综述强调,缺乏细胞水平病毒读取分配、病原学匹配对照的患者水平分析、空间或纵向采样以及正交验证的研究信息量较少,并且可能导致不一致的结论。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了从 HPV 相关癌症的细胞分辨病毒 宿主 程序中产生可重复的生物标志物,未来的研究应将细胞水平病毒读取分配与患者水平分析相结合,包括病原学匹配的对照,采用空间或纵向采样,并纳入正交验证。诸如此类的设计特征对于克服当前的异质性和提高生物标志物的可靠性是必要的。

papers.title: FOCUS: A Dual-Mismatch crRNA Strategy Unlocks High-Fidelity One-Step SNV Detection with Cas12a.
papers.abstract: CRISPR/Cas12a has emerged as a powerful tool for nucleic acid detection; however, its clinical utility is severely hampered by intrinsic limitations in single-nucleotide variant (SNV) discrimination, reliance on pre-processed single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) templates, and cumbersome multi-step workflows. Here, we report a novel molecular design principle by engineering crRNAs with site-specific dual mismatches (positions 12 and 14 relative to the PAM), which we systematically demonstrate to drastically enhance the SNV discrimination capability of Cas12a. Leveraging this breakthrough, we developed FOCUS (Fast One-step CRISPR-based Universalizable SNV detection system), an all-in-one CRISPR sensing platform that enables isothermal detection of SNVs from double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) by integrating amplification and detection in a single reaction system. FOCUS achieved attomolar-level sensitivity (13.15 aM) and ultrafast readout (< 20 min) for distinguishing the highly homologous survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) and SMN2 genes-the gold standard challenge for SNV genotyping in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) diagnostics. To validate its clinical translatability, FOCUS was successfully adapted to a low-cost, equipment-free assay using lateral flow strips and UV visualization, facilitating point-of-care testing (POCT). In a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, FOCUS exhibited 100% diagnostic concordance with gold-standard methods for SMA (21 samples), high-risk HPV 16/18 (27 samples), Staphylococcus aureus (20 samples), and SARS-CoV-2 (107 samples). Collectively, our study establishes a generalizable engineering strategy for Cas12a crRNAs and presents FOCUS as a robust, versatile, and field-deployable solution for precision SNV genotyping, underscoring the translational medicine value of FOCUS in molecular diagnostics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of CRISPR/Cas12a in detecting single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with high fidelity, particularly in clinical settings where accurate SNV discrimination is critical for diagnosing diseases like high-risk HPV infections. The background highlights that CRISPR/Cas12a's clinical utility is hampered by its inability to distinguish SNVs effectively.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, including those from high-risk HPV 16/18, to assess the performance of the FOCUS platform. The samples were collected from various sources and tested for their ability to detect SNVs associated with these HPV types.
analysis.methods: The methods included the development of FOCUS, a CRISPR-based platform that integrates amplification and detection in a single reaction system. analysis.main_results: FOCUS demonstrated 100% diagnostic concordance with gold-standard methods for high-risk HPV 16/18, indicating its effectiveness in accurately detecting SNVs in these contexts.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as a demonstration of a novel molecular design principle that enhances the SNV discrimination capability of Cas12a through site-specific dual mismatches in crRNAs. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have important implications for improving the accuracy and efficiency of SNV detection in HPV-related diagnostics, which can aid in early detection and management of high-risk HPV infections and associated diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, which provides moderate confidence in the performance of FOCUS for high-risk HPV detection. analysis.summary_en: This study introduces FOCUS, a CRISPR-based platform designed to enhance the detection of single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) in high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infections. The research addresses the limitations of CRISPR/Cas12a in clinical settings, particularly its poor SNV discrimination and reliance on pre-processed DNA templates. The study demonstrates that FOCUS achieves high diagnostic accuracy for HPV 16/18, with 100% concordance with gold-standard methods. The platform integrates amplification and detection in a single reaction system, enabling point-of-care testing (POCT) without the need for specialized equipment. The findings suggest that FOCUS could improve the precision and efficiency of HPV-related diagnostics, offering a versatile solution for SNV genotyping. However, the study's evidence is based on a limited set of clinical samples, which may affect the generalisability of the results. The authors present their work as a novel engineering strategy for Cas12a crRNAs, highlighting its potential for translational medicine applications.

papers.title: Somatic alterations in TP53, PIK3CA, and CCND1 reveal exposure-driven patterns in oral and oropharyngeal tumors.
papers.abstract: Abstract Tobacco, alcohol, and human papillomavirus (HPV) are major risk factors for oral cavity (OC) and oropharyngeal (OPC) cancers, yet their specific contributions to the tumor molecular landscape remain incompletely understood. We analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 tumors (606 OC, 480 OPC, including 287 HPV(+)OPC) profiled with a 1,109-gene panel and evaluated their associations with exposures. PIK3CA alterations were widespread but context-specific: HPV(+)OPC featured APOBEC-driven mutations and co-occurrence of FGFR3 mutations in a subset of cases, while HPV(-)OPC and OC were marked by 3q26/28 (PIK3CA/TP63/SOX2) amplifications. analysis.research_question_and_background: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers are linked to tobacco, alcohol, and human papillomavirus (HPV), but the specific contributions of these exposures to tumor molecular alterations remain unclear and require molecular characterization to inform risk stratification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 oral cavity and oropharyngeal tumors (606 oral cavity, 480 oropharyngeal, including 287 HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers) using a 1,109-gene panel to evaluate associations with exposures.
analysis.methods: Tumor samples were profiled with a 1,109-gene panel to identify somatic alterations, and associations between molecular alterations and exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV status were statistically evaluated.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform surveillance strategies and risk stratification by linking specific molecular alterations to known exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV infection in oral and oropharyngeal cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single cohort analyzed with a targeted gene panel and lacks functional validation, which constrains causal inference and generalizability to broader populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 oral cavity and oropharyngeal tumors, including 287 HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers, using a 1,109-gene panel to assess associations with exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV status. These findings define a molecular framework that may inform etiologic-based risk stratification in head and neck cancer, potentially guiding surveillance and prevention strategies tailored to exposure profiles.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:烟草、酒精和人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是口腔癌(OC)和口咽癌(OPC)的主要危险因素,但它们对肿瘤分子景观的具体贡献尚未完全明确。我们分析了1,086例肿瘤(606例OC、480例OPC,其中包括287例HPV阳性OPC)的体细胞突变,这些肿瘤采用包含1,109个基因的检测面板进行分析,并评估了这些突变与暴露因素的关联。PIK3CA突变广泛存在,但具有情境特异性:HPV阳性OPC以APOBEC驱动的突变和FGFR3突变的共发为特征,而HPV阴性OPC和OC则以3q26/28(PIK3CA/TP63/SOX2)扩增为标志。TP53是HPV阴性肿瘤中突变频率最高的基因,在HPV阴性OPC中,吸烟者的TP53突变频率显著升高,而在OC中,无论吸烟状态如何,TP53突变频率均保持高位。CCND1扩增主要局限于HPV阴性肿瘤,且在报告同时使用烟草和酒精的个体中最为常见。这种联合效应在TCGA口腔癌-口咽癌数据集中得到复现,并在转录组水平上得到反映,即CCND1 mRNA表达在双重使用者中最高。在OC中,对至今最大的来自从未吸烟-从未饮酒患者的肿瘤队列(N=100)进行特征分析,发现这些患者更可能来自女性,且与既往吸烟-饮酒患者(N=353)相比,FAT1和CASP8突变更为富集。综上所述,这些发现界定了按亚部位和HPV状态划分的暴露驱动型体细胞突变模式,并为基于病因学的头颈部癌症风险分层提供了分子框架。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 口腔癌和口咽癌与烟草、酒精和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 有关,但这些暴露对肿瘤分子改变的具体贡献仍不清楚,需要分子表征来告知风险分层。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究使用 1,109 个基因组分析了 1,086 个口腔和口咽肿瘤(606 个口腔肿瘤,480 个口咽肿瘤,包括 287 个 HPV 阳性口咽癌)的体细胞改变,以评估与暴露的关联。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过 1,109 个基因组对肿瘤样本进行分析,以识别体细胞改变,并对分子改变与烟草、酒精和 HPV 状态等暴露之间的关联进行统计评估。
analysis_zh.main_results: PIK3CA 改变很常见,但与具体情况有关:HPV 阳性口咽癌显示 APOBEC 驱动的 突变 和 FGFR3 共现,而 HPV 阴性肿瘤和口腔癌则显示 3q26/28 扩增;TP53 在 HPV 阴性肿瘤中最常发生突变,在 HPV 阴性口咽癌吸烟者中最为常见。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究通过肿瘤亚位点和 HPV 状态定义了不同的、暴露驱动的体细胞改变模式,提供了一个分子框架,可以指导头颈癌基于病因的风险分层。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以通过将特定的分子改变与口腔癌和口咽癌中的烟草、酒精和 HPV 感染等已知暴露联系起来,为 监测 策略和风险分层提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于使用目标基因组分析的单个 队列研究,并且缺乏功能验证,这限制了因果推断和对更广泛人群的推广。

papers.title: Cervical mixed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and adenocarcinoma with genital tract dissemination: a case report and literature review
papers.abstract: Background Primary mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) of the cervix are exceedingly rare. This report describes a case of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical MiNEN composed of adenocarcinoma and small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) of cervix. Clinical and pathological findings suggest that the adenocarcinoma component extended to the endometrium, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries via genital tract dissemination. Case presentation A 48-year-old female presented with abnormal vaginal discharge for more than eight months and HPV genotyping test was positive for type 18. Pelvic MRI revealed cervical space-occupying lesions and cystic changes in the adnexal region. Gross examination revealed an ulcerative cervical mass, thickened and dilated fallopian tubes, and polycystic ovaries. The tumor was solid, and the cut surface was grayish white with mucus. Histologically, the cervical tumor comprised 65% SCNEC and 35% HPV-associated adenocarcinoma, both of which diffusely expressed p16. Adenocarcinoma was identified in the endometrium and bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries, and its morphology, immunophenotype, and HPV infection status were consistent with those of cervical adenocarcinoma, suggesting that the cervical adenocarcinoma disseminated along the reproductive tract. Despite receiving systemic chemotherapy and local radiotherapy following surgery, the patient unfortunately passed away due to the progression of the disease in November 2022. Conclusions Cervical MiNENs are highly aggressive malignancies associated with poor prognoses. HPV-associated tumors may spread contiguously through the reproductive tract, mimicking primary tumors of the endometrium, fallopian tubes, or ovaries. Accurate diagnosis and effective management of patients rely on meticulous postoperative histopathological evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on cervical mixed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and adenocarcinoma with genital tract dissemination, specifically examining the role of human papillomavirus (HPV) in these malignancies. The central question is whether HPV-associated tumors can spread contiguously through the reproductive tract, mimicking primary tumors of the endometrium, fallopian tubes, or ovaries.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report and literature review. It does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or meta-analysis. The evidence is derived from a single case and general observations from the literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that cervical MiNENs are highly aggressive malignancies associated with poor prognoses. It also highlights that HPV-associated tumors may spread contiguously through the reproductive tract, potentially mimicking primary tumors in other genital tract sites.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the spread of HPV-associated tumors through the genital tract is not well understood, and there is limited evidence on the mechanisms of dissemination. The case described is unique, and further studies are needed to confirm these findings in a broader context.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of accurate diagnosis and effective management of patients with cervical MiNENs, which requires meticulous postoperative histopathological evaluation. It also suggests the need for more research on the behavior and spread of HPV-associated tumors in the genital tract.

analysis.summary_en: This review presents a case report of a 48-year-old female with cervical mixed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and adenocarcinoma associated with HPV type 18. The tumor extended to the endometrium, fallopian tubes, and ovaries through genital tract dissemination. Histopathological findings showed the tumor was composed of 65% SCNEC and 35% HPV-associated adenocarcinoma, both expressing p16. Despite treatment, the patient died in November 2022. The review concludes that cervical MiNENs are aggressive and have poor prognoses, and that HPV-associated tumors may spread contiguously through the reproductive tract, mimicking primary tumors in other sites. It highlights the need for detailed histopathological evaluation and further research on the mechanisms of HPV-related tumor dissemination.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注宫颈混合性小细胞神经内分泌癌和伴有生殖道播散的腺癌,特别研究了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 在这些恶性肿瘤中的作用。核心问题是 HPV 相关肿瘤是否可以通过生殖道连续扩散,模仿子宫内膜、输卵管或卵巢的原发性肿瘤。

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,宫颈 MiNEN 是一种高度侵袭性的恶性肿瘤,预后不良。它还强调,HPV 相关肿瘤可能通过生殖道连续扩散,可能模仿其他生殖道部位的原发性肿瘤。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,HPV 相关肿瘤通过生殖道的传播尚不清楚,并且关于传播机制的证据有限。所描述的案例是独特的,需要进一步的研究来在更广泛的背景下证实这些发现。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了准确的 诊断 和对颈部 MiNEN 患者有效管理的重要性,这需要细致的术后组织病理学评估。它还表明需要对生殖道中 HPV 相关肿瘤的行为和传播进行更多研究。

papers.title: Case report: Penile collision tumor comprising HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma and malignant melanoma
papers.abstract: Collision tumors with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and malignant melanoma components are extremely rare. We report a case of a penile collision tumor with a component of HPV-associated SCC and malignant melanoma in a 61 year-old man. The patient underwent a partial penectomy and bilateral inguinal sentinel lymph node surgery. Microscopy showed a biphasic tumor with a component of SCC with warty-basaloid morphology, positive for HPV16 and 43, and a malignant melanoma associated with a BRAF mutation. This case posed diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to the absence of a precise TNM classification and documented treatment guidelines for this tumor type.
